pub mod parse;
//! # The slot: LZ77 parsing.
//!
//! This whole file is what a miner replaces. It must be compilable as its own
//! crate root (`charon rustc … src/parse.rs`), so it may not `use crate::…`.
//!
//! ## The contract
//!
//! `parse` reads `input` and writes a token stream into `out`, returning how many
//! tokens it wrote. A token is a `u32`:
//!
//! * `t < 256`                           — emit the literal byte `t`
//! * `t = 2^24 + (dist-1)*256 + (len-3)` — copy `len` bytes from `dist` back
//!
//! with `1 ≤ dist ≤ 32768` and `3 ≤ len ≤ 258`. The arithmetic encoding (rather
//! than shifts and masks) is deliberate: `Nat` `+`, `*`, `/` and `%` are what
//! `omega` reasons about on the Lean side, and `&&&`/`<<<` are not.
//!
//! The only thing that must be proved is that the token stream **decodes back to
//! `input`**, and that `parse` neither panics nor diverges.
//!
//! ## What is *not* constrained
//!
//! Nothing about the search. The hash chains below could be a suffix automaton, a
//! binary tree, or a full optimal-parse dynamic program and the proof would not
//! grow, because correctness rests only on the bytes `match_len` actually
//! compared before a match was emitted. `hash3_spec` in the proof says the hash
//! lands in range and says nothing whatever about what it computes.
//!
//! ## Prover-friendly Rust — the rules
//!
//! 1. No labelled `break`/`continue`, no early `return` from a nested loop, no
//!    trait objects, no iterator adapters. Indices, `while`, and plain `if`.
//! 2. Prefer `i <= n - k` to `i + k <= n`. In the extracted model a slice may
//!    have length `usize::MAX`, and then the *addition* overflows and the program
//!    is not total. The guarded subtraction cannot.
//! 3. Bound every array index with `%`, not `&`. `h % 32768 < 32768` is one
//!    `omega` step; the same fact about `h & 0x7fff` is a bitvector argument.
//! 4. Give every loop a decreasing counter that does not depend on the data. The
//!    chain walk below terminates because `probes` increases, not because the
//!    chain is acyclic — which it need not be.

pub const MIN_MATCH: usize = 3;
pub const MAX_MATCH: usize = 258;
pub const WINDOW: usize = 32768;
pub const HASH_SIZE: usize = 32768;

/// How far down a hash chain to look. The whole speed/ratio dial.
pub const MAX_PROBES: usize = 16;

/// Hash of the three bytes at a position. Any function of the right range works;
/// `% 32768` rather than `& 0x7fff` so that the index bound is arithmetic.
pub fn hash3(a: u8, b: u8, c: u8) -> usize {
    let x = (a as u32)
        .wrapping_mul(2654435761)
        .wrapping_add((b as u32).wrapping_mul(2246822519))
        .wrapping_add((c as u32).wrapping_mul(3266489917));
    ((x >> 15) % 32768) as usize
}

/// How many bytes match at `a` and `b`, up to `cap`. This is the *only* function
/// whose result the correctness proof depends on.
pub fn match_len(input: &[u8], a: usize, b: usize, cap: usize) -> usize {
    let mut l = 0usize;
    while l < cap && input[b + l] == input[a + l] {
        l += 1;
    }
    l
}

/// Walk a hash chain and return the best `(length, distance)` it finds.
///
/// A separate function rather than a loop inside `parse`, and that is **not**
/// cosmetic: Aeneas reports `Unimplemented` for a second loop nested in the body
/// of `parse`'s outer loop when that loop also reads a local array of the
/// enclosing scope. Lifting it out, with the array as a `&[u32]` parameter,
/// translates. Prover-friendly rule 5.
///
/// `prev` must be at least 32768 long; `parse` passes a `[u32; 32768]`.
pub fn find_match(
    input: &[u8],
    prev: &[u32],
    pos: usize,
    cap: usize,
    start: usize,
) -> (usize, usize) {
    let mut best_len = 0usize;
    let mut best_dist = 0usize;
    let mut cur = start;
    let mut probes = 0usize;
    while probes < 16 && cur > 0 && cur <= pos {
        let cpos = cur - 1;
        if pos - cpos <= 32768 {
            let l = match_len(input, cpos, pos, cap);
            if l > best_len {
                best_len = l;
                best_dist = pos - cpos;
            }
            cur = prev[cpos % 32768] as usize;
        } else {
            // Everything further down the chain is older still, so the walk is
            // over. `cur = 0` ends it without a `break`.
            cur = 0;
        }
        probes += 1;
    }
    (best_len, best_dist)
}

/// Greedy matching over hash chains.
///
/// `head[h]` is the most recent position whose three bytes hash to `h`, plus one
/// (zero means "none"). `prev[p % 32768]` is the position before `p` in the same
/// chain, plus one. The `+ 1` is what lets zero be the sentinel without a
/// separate occupancy array, and `% 32768` keeps `prev` a fixed-size array rather
/// than one allocation per input.
pub fn parse(input: &[u8], out: &mut [u32]) -> usize {
    let n = input.len();
    let mut head = [0u32; 32768];
    let mut prev = [0u32; 32768];
    let mut ntok = 0usize;
    let mut pos = 0usize;
    let has3 = n >= 3;
    let lim = if has3 { n - 3 } else { 0 };
    while pos < n {
        let mut best_len = 0usize;
        let mut best_dist = 0usize;
        if has3 && pos <= lim {
            let h = hash3(input[pos], input[pos + 1], input[pos + 2]);
            let start = head[h] as usize;
            prev[pos % 32768] = head[h];
            head[h] = (pos + 1) as u32;

            let mut cap = n - pos;
            if cap > 258 {
                cap = 258;
            }
            // The chain walk. It terminates on `probes`, never on the chain
            // being acyclic — a truncated `as u32` can point anywhere, and the
            // byte comparison inside `match_len` is what keeps that harmless.
            let found = find_match(input, &prev, pos, cap, start);
            best_len = found.0;
            best_dist = found.1;
        }
        if best_len >= 3 {
            out[ntok] = 16777216u32 + ((best_dist - 1) as u32) * 256 + ((best_len - 3) as u32);
            ntok += 1;
            let end = pos + best_len;
            let mut k = pos + 1;
            while k < end && has3 && k <= lim {
                let h2 = hash3(input[k], input[k + 1], input[k + 2]);
                prev[k % 32768] = head[h2];
                head[h2] = (k + 1) as u32;
                k += 1;
            }
            pos = end;
        } else {
            out[ntok] = input[pos] as u32;
            ntok += 1;
            pos += 1;
        }
    }
    ntok
}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build the scoring corpus.

Four files, deliberately different in kind, because a corpus of one kind measures
one kind of parse. `docs/EXP2_REAL_CODE.md`'s trap applies directly: the first
headroom run in this project used repetitive synthetic data, compressed 300:1,
and reported a conclusion that was backwards.

In a real round this is held out and commit-revealed, and only *shape* statistics
are published. Here it is reproducible on purpose, so that the numbers in the docs
can be checked.
"""
import hashlib
import pathlib
import sys

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / "corpus"

# (name, roots, extensions, cap in bytes)
PARTS = [
    ("source.rs.txt",
     ["../../probes", "../slot", "../harness", "../../../conjectures-rust/crates",
      "../../../conjectures-rust/verifier", "../../../conjectures-validator/conjectures_subnet"],
     {".rs", ".toml", ".py"}, 2_000_000),
    ("prose.md.txt",
     ["../../docs", "../..", "../../../conjectures-rust/docs",
      "../../../conjectures-rust", "../../../conjectures-validator/docs"],
     {".md"}, 2_000_000),
    ("lean.txt",
     ["../lean/Lz77", "../lean/Slot", "../lean/Proof",
      "../../probes/real-kernel/Sort", "../../probes/aeneas-reach/Proof",
      "../../../conjectures-rust/lean"],
     {".lean"}, 2_000_000),
    ("json.txt",
     ["../../../conjectures-rust/tasks", "../../../conjectures-rust",
      "../../probes/real-kernel"],
     {".json", ".lock"}, 1_000_000),
    ("binary.bin", ["../harness/target/release", "../slot/target/release"],
     {"", ".rlib"}, 2_000_000),
]


def collect(roots, exts, cap):
    buf = bytearray()
    for r in roots:
        base = (ROOT / "verifier" / r).resolve()
        if not base.exists():
            continue
        for p in sorted(base.rglob("*")):
            if len(buf) >= cap:
                break
            if not p.is_file() or p.suffix not in exts:
                continue
            if ".lake" in p.parts or "packages" in p.parts:
                continue
            try:
                b = p.read_bytes()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if len(b) > 4_000_000:
                continue
            buf += b
    return bytes(buf[:cap])


def main():
    OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    total = 0
    print(f"{'file':<18} {'bytes':>10}  sha256")
    for name, roots, exts, cap in PARTS:
        data = collect(roots, exts, cap)
        if len(data) < 4096:
            print(f"{name:<18} {'SKIPPED':>10}  (nothing found under {roots})")
            continue
        (OUT / name).write_bytes(data)
        total += len(data)
        print(f"{name:<18} {len(data):>10}  {hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()[:16]}")
    print(f"{'TOTAL':<18} {total:>10}")
    if total == 0:
        sys.exit("corpus is empty")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The submission gate.

    ./verifier/verify.py            check the working tree
    ./verifier/verify.py --pin      rewrite verifier/PINS.json from the tree

Six stages, and **the order is the design**. Nothing is compiled for speed and
nothing is timed until the proof has been accepted, so a submission cannot buy
validator time with a program that does not have a proof — the lesson v1's
`docs/VERIFIER.md` records, carried over unchanged.

    1  policy      the submitted Rust is inside the prover-friendly subset
    2  pins        only the two files a miner owns have changed
    3  extract     the verifier runs charon+aeneas ITSELF on the submitted Rust
    4  statement   `LZ77.Obligation slot.parse` typechecks from the miner's proof
    5  axioms      nothing beyond propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound
    6  score       only now: build, round-trip, compressed bytes, speed floor

Stage 3 is the one that is easy to get wrong. An extraction that arrives inside a
submission is worthless — it is a claim about a program, made by the person whose
program it is. The verifier regenerates it.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
LEAN = ROOT / "lean"
ELAN = os.environ.get(
    "ELAN_HOME", "/home/robert/repos/s66_repositories/conjectures-validator/.elan"
)

#: The only two files a submission may change.
MINER_OWNED = ["slot/src/parse.rs", "lean/Proof/Parse.lean"]

#: Everything else that participates in the verdict, pinned by hash.
PINNED = [
    "lean/Lz77/Spec.lean",
    "lean/Lz77/Lemmas.lean",
    "lean/Lz77/Interface.lean",
    "lean/Lz77.lean",
    "lean/Verify/Obligation.lean",
    "lean/Verify.lean",
    "lean/Proof/Axioms.lean",
    "lean/lakefile.toml",
    "lean/lean-toolchain",
    "lean/lake-manifest.json",
    "harness/src/deflate.rs",
    "harness/src/token.rs",
    "harness/src/baseline.rs",
    "harness/src/main.rs",
    "harness/Cargo.toml",
    "verifier/verify.py",
    "verifier/extract.sh",
    "verifier/make-corpus.py",
]

ALLOWED_AXIOMS = {"propext", "Classical.choice", "Quot.sound"}

#: Prover-friendly Rust, enforced. Each entry is (regex, why it is rejected).
#: A miner who discovers these by failing is a miner who leaves, so they are also
#: documented with a worked example in `docs/MINER.md`.
POLICY = [
    (r"\bunsafe\b", "`unsafe` is outside the translated subset"),
    (r"'[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z_0-9]*\s*:\s*(?:while|loop|for)\b",
     "labelled loops: Aeneas cannot translate labelled break/continue"),
    (r"\b(?:break|continue)\s+'", "labelled break/continue"),
    (r"\bfor\b\s+\w+\s+\bin\b", "`for` loops go through Iterator, which is opaque"),
    (r"\.iter\(\)|\.into_iter\(\)|\.chunks\(|\.windows\(|\.fold\(|\.map\(|\.filter\(",
     "iterator adapters are opaque; use indices"),
    (r"\bdyn\b|\bimpl\s+(?:Fn|Iterator)", "trait objects and impl-trait are opaque"),
    (r"\buse\s+crate::", "the slot is compiled as its own crate root"),
    (r"\bstd::arch|core::arch|_mm_|__m128|__m256|target_feature",
     "SIMD is outside the subset (and cannot improve ratio anyway)"),
    (r"\bextern\b|\basm!|\binclude!", "no foreign code"),
    (r"\bstatic\s+mut\b", "mutable statics"),
]


def sha(p: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def fail(stage: str, msg: str) -> None:
    print(f"\nREJECTED at stage {stage}\n  {msg}")
    sys.exit(1)


def run(cmd, **kw):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["ELAN_HOME"] = ELAN
    env["PATH"] = f"{ELAN}/bin:" + env["PATH"]
    return subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, **kw)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def stage_policy() -> None:
    src = (ROOT / "slot/src/parse.rs").read_text()
    # Strip comments so a rule named in a doc comment is not a violation.
    stripped = re.sub(r"//[^\n]*", "", src)
    stripped = re.sub(r"/\*.*?\*/", "", stripped, flags=re.S)
    bad = []
    for pattern, why in POLICY:
        for m in re.finditer(pattern, stripped):
            line = stripped[: m.start()].count("\n") + 1
            bad.append(f"line ~{line}: {m.group(0)!r} — {why}")
    if bad:
        fail("1 (policy)", "\n  ".join(bad))
    print("1 policy      ok — the submitted Rust is inside the subset")


def stage_pins(rewrite: bool) -> None:
    pins_file = ROOT / "verifier/PINS.json"
    current = {p: sha(ROOT / p) for p in PINNED if (ROOT / p).exists()}
    if rewrite:
        pins_file.write_text(json.dumps(current, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
        print(f"wrote {pins_file.relative_to(ROOT)} ({len(current)} files)")
        return
    if not pins_file.exists():
        fail("2 (pins)", "verifier/PINS.json is missing; run --pin")
    pinned = json.loads(pins_file.read_text())
    changed = [p for p in pinned if current.get(p) != pinned[p]]
    missing = [p for p in pinned if p not in current]
    if changed or missing:
        fail(
            "2 (pins)",
            "a submission may change only "
            + ", ".join(MINER_OWNED)
            + "\n  changed: "
            + ", ".join(changed + missing),
        )
    print(f"2 pins        ok — {len(pinned)} contract and harness files unchanged")


def stage_extract() -> None:
    r = run([str(ROOT / "verifier/extract.sh")])
    if r.returncode != 0:
        fail("3 (extract)", (r.stderr or r.stdout).strip()[:2000])
    print("3 extract     ok — charon+aeneas re-run by the verifier, no new axioms")


def stage_build() -> str:
    r = run(["lake", "build", "Verify"], cwd=LEAN)
    out = r.stdout + r.stderr
    if r.returncode != 0:
        errs = [l for l in out.splitlines() if l.startswith("error")]
        fail("4 (statement)", "\n  ".join(errs[:20]) or out.strip()[-2000:])
    print("4 statement   ok — `LZ77.Obligation slot.parse` typechecks")
    return out


def stage_axioms(build_output: str) -> None:
    line = next(
        (l for l in build_output.splitlines() if "'accepted' depends on axioms" in l),
        None,
    )
    if line is None:
        # A cached build does not re-emit the message; force it.
        (LEAN / "Verify/Obligation.lean").touch()
        line = next(
            (
                l
                for l in stage_build().splitlines()
                if "'accepted' depends on axioms" in l
            ),
            None,
        )
    if line is None:
        fail("5 (axioms)", "no axiom report was produced")
    names = set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9.]*", line.split("[", 1)[1]))
    extra = names - ALLOWED_AXIOMS
    if extra:
        fail("5 (axioms)", f"the proof rests on {sorted(extra)}")
    print(f"5 axioms      ok — {sorted(ALLOWED_AXIOMS)}")


def stage_score() -> int:
    for crate in ("slot", "harness"):
        r = run(["cargo", "build", "--release", "-q"], cwd=ROOT / crate)
        if r.returncode != 0:
            fail("6 (score)", f"{crate} does not build:\n{r.stderr[-2000:]}")
    corpus = ROOT / "corpus"
    if not corpus.exists() or not any(corpus.iterdir()):
        fail("6 (score)", "corpus is empty; run verifier/make-corpus.py")
    r = run([str(ROOT / "harness/target/release/harness"), str(corpus)])
    print("6 score       running…\n")
    print(r.stdout.rstrip())
    if r.returncode != 0:
        print(r.stderr.rstrip())
    return r.returncode


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--pin", action="store_true", help="rewrite PINS.json from the tree")
    ap.add_argument("--no-score", action="store_true", help="stop after the proof gate")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if args.pin:
        stage_pins(rewrite=True)
        return

    print("verifying submission\n")
    stage_policy()
    stage_pins(rewrite=False)
    stage_extract()
    out = stage_build()
    stage_axioms(out)
    if args.no_score:
        print("\nproof accepted (scoring skipped)")
        return
    sys.exit(stage_score())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
[package]
name = "aeneas_reach"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
path = "src/lib.rs"
# Proof-cost probe. Separate package because Aeneas's Lean library needs Mathlib
# and pins its own toolchain; nothing here is meant to ship.
name = "reach"
defaultTargets = ["Reach"]

[[require]]
name = "aeneas"
git = "https://github.com/AeneasVerif/aeneas"
rev = "nightly-2026.08.27-5b9dcf3"
subDir = "backends/lean"

# Generated by `charon` + `aeneas` from src/lib.rs. Never hand-edited.
[[lean_lib]]
name = "Reach"

# The proofs. Kept out of the generated tree so `charon`+`aeneas` can regenerate
# `Reach/` without touching them.
[[lean_lib]]
name = "Proof"
//! Twelve patterns drawn from real Rust performance work, one function each.
//!
//! The question this crate exists to answer: **which shapes of optimisation code
//! can Charon and Aeneas actually translate into Lean?** That is the gating
//! constraint on any competition where miners submit Rust patches and pay for
//! them with a proof, because a patch outside the translated subset cannot be
//! proved at all -- and the previous project learned the hard way that guessing
//! about tool reach is a mistake. Each function is deliberately trivial so that a
//! failure is a fact about the *shape*, not about the difficulty.
//!
//! Grouped by what a real patch would look like.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 1-3. Indexed loops over slices. The skeleton of nearly every hot loop.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The plainest possible accumulate-over-slice loop.
pub fn sum_indexed(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    let mut total: u32 = 0;
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < xs.len() {
        total = total.wrapping_add(xs[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    total
}

/// Search with early return: `memchr`, `find`, and every scan loop.
pub fn find_byte(xs: &[u8], needle: u8) -> Option<usize> {
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < xs.len() {
        if xs[i] == needle {
            return Some(i);
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    None
}

/// Four-at-a-time unrolling: one of the most common hand optimisations there is,
/// and the shape a miner would submit to speed up a scan.
pub fn sum_unrolled(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    let mut total: u32 = 0;
    let n = xs.len();
    let limit = n - n % 4;
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < limit {
        total = total
            .wrapping_add(xs[i])
            .wrapping_add(xs[i + 1])
            .wrapping_add(xs[i + 2])
            .wrapping_add(xs[i + 3]);
        i += 4;
    }
    while i < n {
        total = total.wrapping_add(xs[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    total
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 4-5. Bit manipulation and table lookup: decoders, hashes, encoders.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Word-at-a-time bit tricks. `count_ones`/`leading_zeros` are intrinsics, so
/// this also probes whether Aeneas has models for them.
pub fn bit_tricks(x: u64) -> u32 {
    let folded = x ^ (x >> 32);
    folded.count_ones() + (folded.leading_zeros() >> 1)
}

/// A const lookup table, indexed by a byte. Hex decode, base64, UTF-8
/// classification, character classes -- all of this shape.
static HEX: [u8; 16] = [
    b'0', b'1', b'2', b'3', b'4', b'5', b'6', b'7', b'8', b'9', b'a', b'b', b'c', b'd', b'e', b'f',
];

pub fn nibble_to_hex(n: u8) -> u8 {
    HEX[(n & 0xf) as usize]
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 6-7. Mutation through a slice, and swapping: sorting and in-place transforms.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// In-place write through `&mut [T]`.
pub fn increment_all(xs: &mut [u32]) {
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < xs.len() {
        xs[i] = xs[i].wrapping_add(1);
        i += 1;
    }
}

/// Insertion sort: the small-input case of every real sort, including Rust's own
/// `driftsort`. If this translates, "prove your sort sorts" is on the table.
pub fn insertion_sort(xs: &mut [u32]) {
    let mut i = 1usize;
    while i < xs.len() {
        let mut j = i;
        while j > 0 && xs[j - 1] > xs[j] {
            let tmp = xs[j - 1];
            xs[j - 1] = xs[j];
            xs[j] = tmp;
            j -= 1;
        }
        i += 1;
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 8-9. Allocation and growth: any patch that builds output.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn collect_doubled(xs: &[u32]) -> Vec<u32> {
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(xs.len());
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < xs.len() {
        out.push(xs[i].wrapping_mul(2));
        i += 1;
    }
    out
}

/// Structural recursion over an enum. Known to work -- `Rel::width` in the v1
/// project. Included as the positive control: if this fails, the harness is
/// broken rather than the pattern.
pub enum Tree {
    Leaf(u32),
    Node(Box<Tree>, Box<Tree>),
}

pub fn tree_sum(t: &Tree) -> u32 {
    match t {
        Tree::Leaf(v) => *v,
        Tree::Node(l, r) => tree_sum(l).wrapping_add(tree_sum(r)),
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// 10-12. Iterator adapters and closures. Expected to fail; measuring how badly.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub fn sum_iterator(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    xs.iter().fold(0u32, |a, b| a.wrapping_add(*b))
}

pub fn sum_chunked(xs: &[u32]) -> u32 {
    let mut total = 0u32;
    for chunk in xs.chunks(4) {
        for v in chunk {
            total = total.wrapping_add(*v);
        }
    }
    total
}

/// Two slices at once: comparison, `memcmp`, and merge steps.
pub fn common_prefix(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> usize {
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < a.len() && i < b.len() && a[i] == b[i] {
        i += 1;
    }
    i
}

//! Is compressed size a deterministic metric? If it is, the measurement problem
//! that sank the v1 design disappears: two validators on different hardware
//! compute the identical integer, so the ladder needs no pinned CPU governor, no
//! isolated cores, no variance gate and no trimmed median.
fn main() {
    let data = std::fs::read("corpus.bin").unwrap();
    for level in [1u8, 6, 9] {
        let sizes: Vec<usize> = (0..5)
            .map(|_| miniz_oxide::deflate::compress_to_vec(&data, level).len())
            .collect();
        let a = miniz_oxide::deflate::compress_to_vec(&data, level);
        let b = miniz_oxide::deflate::compress_to_vec(&data, level);
        println!(
            "level {level}: sizes {:?} all_equal={} bytes_identical={}",
            sizes,
            sizes.iter().all(|s| *s == sizes[0]),
            a == b
        );
    }
}
//! Experiment 1: is the level-1 ratio gap reachable without SIMD?
//!
//! `create_comp_flags_from_zip_params` gives level 1 exactly two handicaps:
//! `NUM_PROBES[1] == 1`, so `find_match` inspects a single hash-chain position,
//! and `TDEFL_GREEDY_PARSING_FLAG`, so there is no lazy matching. Both are the
//! classic non-SIMD levers. Before writing any new code, ask the cheaper
//! question: does the *existing* algorithm, re-parameterised, close the gap?
//!
//! If it does, the headroom is real and algorithmic. If it does not, the gap is
//! somewhere else and the recommendation is wrong.
use miniz_oxide::deflate::core::{compress_to_output, CompressorOxide, TDEFLFlush, TDEFLStatus};
use std::time::Instant;

const GREEDY: u32 = 0x0000_4000;

fn deflate(data: &[u8], flags: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut c = CompressorOxide::new(flags);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() / 2);
    let (status, _) = compress_to_output(&mut c, data, TDEFLFlush::Finish, |chunk| {
        out.extend_from_slice(chunk);
        true
    });
    assert_eq!(status, TDEFLStatus::Done);
    out
}

fn best_of(reps: u32, data: &[u8], flags: u32) -> (f64, usize) {
    let mut best = f64::MAX;
    let mut size = 0;
    for _ in 0..reps {
        let t = Instant::now();
        size = deflate(data, flags).len();
        best = best.min(t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    }
    (best, size)
}

fn main() {
    let data = std::fs::read("corpus.bin").expect("run `just corpus`");
    let mib = data.len() as f64 / (1 << 20) as f64;

    // The reference points, from `just headroom`.
    let zlib1 = 321_664usize;
    let (base_t, base_s) = best_of(5, &data, 1 | GREEDY); // exactly level 1
    println!("corpus {:.2} MiB", mib);
    println!("zlib level 1 (reference)                     {zlib1} B");
    println!(
        "miniz_oxide level 1  (1 probe, greedy)       {base_s} B  {:+.1}% vs zlib   {:.0} MiB/s",
        100.0 * (base_s as f64 - zlib1 as f64) / zlib1 as f64,
        mib / base_t
    );
    println!();
    println!("--- knob A: deeper hash chain (more probes, still greedy) ---");
    for probes in [2u32, 4, 8, 16, 32] {
        let (t, s) = best_of(3, &data, probes | GREEDY);
        println!(
            "  {probes:3} probes   {s} B  {:+6.1}% vs zlib   {:6.0} MiB/s  ({:.2}x baseline time)",
            100.0 * (s as f64 - zlib1 as f64) / zlib1 as f64,
            mib / t,
            t / base_t
        );
    }
    println!();
    println!("--- knob B: lazy matching (drop the greedy flag) ---");
    for probes in [1u32, 2, 4, 8] {
        let (t, s) = best_of(3, &data, probes);
        println!(
            "  {probes:3} probes   {s} B  {:+6.1}% vs zlib   {:6.0} MiB/s  ({:.2}x baseline time)",
            100.0 * (s as f64 - zlib1 as f64) / zlib1 as f64,
            mib / t,
            t / base_t
        );
    }
}
//! Experiment 1, corrected: the speed/ratio *frontier*, not a single point.
//!
//! The first version of this measurement compared miniz_oxide level 1 against
//! zlib level 1 and reported "15.2% worse compression". That was an unfair
//! comparison: it was also 46% faster. Comparing two different points on a
//! tradeoff curve says nothing about which implementation is better.
//!
//! The honest question is the frontier: at a given speed, who produces the
//! smallest output? And the baseline has to be the state of the art, which for
//! DEFLATE is libdeflate, not the 1995 reference implementation.
use miniz_oxide::deflate::core::{compress_to_output, CompressorOxide, TDEFLFlush, TDEFLStatus};
use std::io::Write;
use std::time::Instant;

const GREEDY: u32 = 0x0000_4000;

fn mo(data: &[u8], flags: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut c = CompressorOxide::new(flags);
    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(data.len() / 2);
    let (s, _) = compress_to_output(&mut c, data, TDEFLFlush::Finish, |ch| {
        out.extend_from_slice(ch);
        true
    });
    assert_eq!(s, TDEFLStatus::Done);
    out
}

fn zlib(data: &[u8], level: u32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut e = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::new(level));
    e.write_all(data).unwrap();
    e.finish().unwrap()
}

fn libdef(data: &[u8], level: i32) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut c = libdeflater::Compressor::new(libdeflater::CompressionLvl::new(level).unwrap());
    let mut out = vec![0u8; c.deflate_compress_bound(data.len())];
    let n = c.deflate_compress(data, &mut out).unwrap();
    out.truncate(n);
    out
}

fn bench(name: String, data: &[u8], f: impl Fn(&[u8]) -> Vec<u8>) -> (String, f64, usize) {
    let mut best = f64::MAX;
    let mut size = 0;
    for _ in 0..4 {
        let t = Instant::now();
        size = f(data).len();
        best = best.min(t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    }
    (name, best, size)
}

fn main() {
    let data = std::fs::read("corpus.bin").expect("run `just corpus`");
    let mib = data.len() as f64 / (1 << 20) as f64;
    let mut rows = Vec::new();

    for p in [1u32, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32] {
        rows.push(bench(format!("miniz_oxide  {p:2} probe greedy"), &data, |d| mo(d, p | GREEDY)));
    }
    for p in [1u32, 4, 8, 32, 128] {
        rows.push(bench(format!("miniz_oxide  {p:2} probe lazy  "), &data, |d| mo(d, p)));
    }
    for l in [1u32, 6, 9] {
        rows.push(bench(format!("zlib         level {l}         "), &data, |d| zlib(d, l)));
    }
    for l in [1i32, 6, 9, 12] {
        rows.push(bench(format!("libdeflate   level {l:2}        "), &data, |d| libdef(d, l)));
    }

    rows.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap());
    println!("corpus {:.2} MiB. Sorted slowest first.\n", mib);
    println!("{:<34} {:>10} {:>10}  {}", "implementation", "MiB/s", "bytes", "on frontier?");

    // A row is on the Pareto frontier if nothing else is both faster and smaller.
    for (name, t, s) in &rows {
        let dominated = rows
            .iter()
            .any(|(_, t2, s2)| (t2 < t && s2 <= s) || (t2 <= t && s2 < s));
        println!(
            "{:<34} {:>10.0} {:>10}  {}",
            name,
            mib / t,
            s,
            if dominated { "" } else { "YES" }
        );
    }
}
//! Is there headroom in miniz_oxide? Compare it against system zlib on the same
//! input, at the same level, checking both produce a stream that inflates back.
use std::io::Write;
use std::time::Instant;

fn corpus() -> Vec<u8> {
    // Real source text, prose and markup. A synthetic repetitive corpus measures
    // nothing: it compresses ~300:1 and the run is dominated by match emission.
    std::fs::read("corpus.bin").expect("run: python3 make-corpus (see justfile)")
}

fn time<F: FnMut() -> usize>(reps: u32, mut f: F) -> (f64, usize) {
    let mut best = f64::MAX;
    let mut size = 0;
    for _ in 0..reps {
        let t = Instant::now();
        size = f();
        best = best.min(t.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
    }
    (best, size)
}

fn main() {
    let data = corpus();
    println!("input {} MiB", data.len() >> 20);
    for level in [1u8, 6, 9] {
        let (mo_t, mo_s) = time(5, || {
            miniz_oxide::deflate::compress_to_vec(&data, level).len()
        });
        let (zl_t, zl_s) = time(5, || {
            let mut e = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(
                Vec::new(),
                flate2::Compression::new(level as u32),
            );
            e.write_all(&data).unwrap();
            e.finish().unwrap().len()
        });
        let mbs = |t: f64| (data.len() as f64 / (1 << 20) as f64) / t;
        println!(
            "level {level}:  miniz_oxide {:6.1} MiB/s ({} B)   zlib {:6.1} MiB/s ({} B)   zlib is {:.2}x faster, {:+.1}% size",
            mbs(mo_t), mo_s, mbs(zl_t), zl_s, mo_t / zl_t,
            100.0 * (mo_s as f64 - zl_s as f64) / zl_s as f64
        );
    }
}

//! `radix_sort_indexed`: the prover-friendly rewrite, and nothing else.
//!
//! Its own module because `Kernel/` is extracted from *this file alone*. The
//! verbatim `radix_sort_symbols` next door cannot come with it: Aeneas emits
//! ill-typed Lean for the `mem::swap` of two `&mut` slices (it destructures a
//! three-tuple out of `core.mem.swap`, which returns a pair), so a `Funs.lean`
//! containing it does not compile at all. See `docs/EXP3_PERMUTATION.md`.
//!
//! `SymFreq` lives here rather than in `original.rs` so that this file has no
//! `use crate::...` and can be compiled as its own crate root by `charon`.
#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
pub struct SymFreq {
    pub key: u16,
    pub sym_index: u16,
}

/// The same radix sort, rewritten in the style a miner would have to submit:
/// indices instead of iterators, and an explicit `bool` saying which buffer
/// holds the result instead of returning one of two `&mut` borrows.
///
/// Behaviourally identical (`tests` below check it against the original). The
/// point is what the *extraction* looks like: no backward-function closure, no
/// iterator state machines, just `Slice.index_usize` and `Slice.update` in
/// `loop`s — the shape `probes/aeneas-reach` showed is cheap to reason about.
pub fn radix_sort_indexed(
    symbols0: &mut [SymFreq],
    symbols1: &mut [SymFreq],
) -> bool {
    let n = symbols0.len();
    let mut hist0 = [0usize; 256];
    let mut hist1 = [0usize; 256];
    let mut i = 0usize;
    while i < n {
        let key = symbols0[i].key;
        hist0[(key & 0xFF) as usize] += 1;
        hist1[((key >> 8) & 0xFF) as usize] += 1;
        i += 1;
    }

    let n_passes = if n == hist1[0] { 1usize } else { 2usize };

    // `in1` tracks which buffer currently holds the data, replacing the
    // `mem::swap` of two `&mut` references that forces Aeneas into a
    // backward-function encoding.
    let mut in1 = false;
    let mut pass = 0usize;
    while pass < n_passes {
        let mut offsets = [0usize; 256];
        let mut offset = 0usize;
        let mut k = 0usize;
        while k < 256 {
            offsets[k] = offset;
            offset += if pass == 0 { hist0[k] } else { hist1[k] };
            k += 1;
        }

        let mut j = 0usize;
        while j < n {
            let sym = if in1 { symbols1[j] } else { symbols0[j] };
            let d = ((sym.key >> (pass * 8)) & 0xFF) as usize;
            let slot = offsets[d];
            if in1 {
                symbols0[slot] = sym;
            } else {
                symbols1[slot] = sym;
            }
            offsets[d] = slot + 1;
            j += 1;
        }
        in1 = !in1;
        pass += 1;
    }
    in1
}
//! Does *real third-party kernel code I did not write* translate, and can the
//! result be proved about?
//!
//! * `original` -- `radix_sort_symbols` verbatim from miniz_oxide.
//! * `indexed`  -- the same sort rewritten the way a miner would have to submit
//!   it, and the subject of the permutation proof in `Sort/`.
//!
//! The test below is the only thing tying the two together: without it, the
//! comparison of extracted shapes compares two different functions.
pub mod indexed;
pub mod original;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use crate::indexed::{radix_sort_indexed, SymFreq};
    use crate::original::radix_sort_symbols;

    /// The rewrite must agree with the original on the same input, or the
    /// comparison of extracted shapes is comparing two different functions.
    #[test]
    fn rewrite_agrees_with_original() {
        for seed in 0u64..200 {
            let mut s = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1);
            let n = (seed as usize % 40) + 1;
            let mk = |s: &mut u64| {
                *s = s.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1);
                SymFreq { key: (*s >> 33) as u16, sym_index: (*s >> 17) as u16 }
            };
            let base: Vec<SymFreq> = (0..n).map(|_| mk(&mut s)).collect();

            let mut a0 = base.clone();
            let mut a1 = vec![SymFreq { key: 0, sym_index: 0 }; n];
            let orig = radix_sort_symbols(&mut a0, &mut a1);
            let orig_keys: Vec<u16> = orig.iter().map(|x| x.key).collect();

            let mut b0 = base.clone();
            let mut b1 = vec![SymFreq { key: 0, sym_index: 0 }; n];
            let in1 = radix_sort_indexed(&mut b0, &mut b1);
            let got = if in1 { &b1 } else { &b0 };
            let got_keys: Vec<u16> = got.iter().map(|x| x.key).collect();

            assert_eq!(orig_keys, got_keys, "n={n} seed={seed}");
            assert!(orig_keys.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] <= w[1]), "not sorted");
        }
    }
}
//! `radix_sort_symbols`, copied VERBATIM from miniz_oxide 0.8.0
//! (src/deflate/core.rs, HuffmanOxide::radix_sort_symbols), with only its
//! enclosing `impl` removed.
//!
//! Kept so the rewrite next door can be checked against it (see the tests in
//! `lib.rs`). Not extracted for proof: it does not survive Aeneas.
use crate::indexed::SymFreq;
use std::mem;

pub fn radix_sort_symbols<'a>(
    symbols0: &'a mut [SymFreq],
    symbols1: &'a mut [SymFreq],
) -> &'a mut [SymFreq] {
    let mut hist = [[0; 256]; 2];

    for freq in symbols0.iter() {
        hist[0][(freq.key & 0xFF) as usize] += 1;
        hist[1][((freq.key >> 8) & 0xFF) as usize] += 1;
    }

    let mut n_passes = 2;
    if symbols0.len() == hist[1][0] {
        n_passes -= 1;
    }

    let mut current_symbols = symbols0;
    let mut new_symbols = symbols1;

    for (pass, hist_item) in hist.iter().enumerate().take(n_passes) {
        let mut offsets = [0; 256];
        let mut offset = 0;
        for i in 0..256 {
            offsets[i] = offset;
            offset += hist_item[i];
        }

        for sym in current_symbols.iter() {
            let j = ((sym.key >> (pass * 8)) & 0xFF) as usize;
            new_symbols[offsets[j]] = *sym;
            offsets[j] += 1;
        }

        mem::swap(&mut current_symbols, &mut new_symbols);
    }

    current_symbols
}

//! One `SessionContext` per arm.
//!
//! The two arms must differ in exactly one thing: whether the miner's rule is
//! in the logical optimizer's rule list. Everything else — config, partition
//! count, the Parquet files, the order tables were registered in — is shared,
//! because any other difference is a confound that shows up as a speedup.

use std::path::Path;
use std::process::Command;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use datafusion::execution::session_state::SessionStateBuilder;
use datafusion::prelude::{ParquetReadOptions, SessionConfig, SessionContext};
use datafusion_optimizer::{Optimizer, OptimizerRule};
use slot_df_rule_host::{LeanRule, RuleStats};

use crate::data::{Dataset, TABLES};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum RulePosition {
    /// After DataFusion's own rules, which is what `docs/STATUS.md` describes:
    /// the rule sees an already-optimised plan and has to find something
    /// DataFusion missed.
    Append,
    /// Before DataFusion's own rules. Worth measuring separately, because a
    /// rule that duplicates `push_down_filter` scores zero when appended and
    /// its true effect is invisible.
    Prepend,
}

impl RulePosition {
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        match s {
            "append" => Ok(Self::Append),
            "prepend" => Ok(Self::Prepend),
            other => Err(format!("unknown rule position {other:?}; expected append or prepend")),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Arm {
    pub name: String,
    pub ctx: SessionContext,
    /// `None` for the champion arm: the baseline champion of a fresh slot is
    /// `Slot.baseline`, the rule that never fires, and not running a host at
    /// all is observationally the same thing and one less variable.
    pub stats: Option<Arc<RuleStats>>,
}

pub struct ArmOptions<'a> {
    pub target_partitions: usize,
    /// Applied to **both** arms. Disabling a DataFusion rule for one arm only
    /// would make the comparison meaningless.
    pub disabled_df_rules: &'a [String],
    pub position: RulePosition,
    pub fuel: u32,
    pub rewrite_timeout: Duration,
}

/// Build an arm. `host` is the already-sandboxed rule host invocation, or
/// `None` for the champion.
pub async fn build(
    name: &str,
    dataset: &Dataset,
    options: &ArmOptions<'_>,
    host: Option<Command>,
) -> Result<Arm, String> {
    build_with(name, dataset, options, host, false).await
}

/// Build an arm whose logical optimizer holds *only* the miner's rule, or
/// nothing at all.
///
/// For the bridge self-check. With DataFusion's own rules in the list the
/// control cannot distinguish "the bridge round trip is broken" from
/// "`push_down_filter` reached the shape first and there was nothing left to
/// rewrite" — and which of those is true is the entire question the control
/// exists to answer.
pub async fn build_isolated(
    name: &str,
    dataset: &Dataset,
    options: &ArmOptions<'_>,
    host: Option<Command>,
) -> Result<Arm, String> {
    build_with(name, dataset, options, host, true).await
}

async fn build_with(
    name: &str,
    dataset: &Dataset,
    options: &ArmOptions<'_>,
    host: Option<Command>,
    isolate: bool,
) -> Result<Arm, String> {
    let mut rules: Vec<Arc<dyn OptimizerRule + Send + Sync>> =
        if isolate { Vec::new() } else { Optimizer::new().rules };

    if !isolate && !options.disabled_df_rules.is_empty() {
        let before = rules.len();
        rules.retain(|r| !options.disabled_df_rules.iter().any(|d| d == r.name()));
        let removed = before - rules.len();
        if removed != options.disabled_df_rules.len() {
            return Err(format!(
                "--disable-df-rule named {} rules but only {removed} matched; \
                 a typo here silently changes what is being measured",
                options.disabled_df_rules.len()
            ));
        }
    }

    let mut stats = None;
    if let Some(command) = host {
        let rule = LeanRule::spawn(format!("{name}_lean_rule"), command, options.fuel)
            .map_err(|e| format!("spawning the rule host: {e}"))?
            .with_timeout(options.rewrite_timeout);
        stats = Some(Arc::clone(&rule.stats));
        let rule: Arc<dyn OptimizerRule + Send + Sync> = Arc::new(rule);
        match options.position {
            RulePosition::Append => rules.push(rule),
            RulePosition::Prepend => rules.insert(0, rule),
        }
    }

    let config = SessionConfig::new()
        .with_target_partitions(options.target_partitions)
        // Fixed rather than inherited so a run is reproducible on a differently
        // sized machine, and identical across arms.
        .with_batch_size(8192)
        .with_information_schema(false);

    let state = SessionStateBuilder::new()
        .with_config(config)
        .with_default_features()
        .with_optimizer_rules(rules)
        .build();
    let ctx = SessionContext::new_with_state(state);

    for table in TABLES {
        let path = dataset.table_path(table);
        register(&ctx, table, &path).await?;
    }

    Ok(Arm { name: name.to_string(), ctx, stats })
}

async fn register(ctx: &SessionContext, table: &str, path: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let url = path.to_str().ok_or_else(|| format!("{}: not valid UTF-8", path.display()))?;
    ctx.register_parquet(table, url, ParquetReadOptions::default())
        .await
        .map_err(|e| format!("registering {table} from {url}: {e}"))
}
//! TPC-H generation, materialised to Parquet once and content-addressed.
//!
//! Both arms must read the same bytes. That is not a stylistic preference: a
//! benchmark where the challenger reads a freshly written file and the champion
//! reads a page-cached one measures the file system. So the data is generated
//! once into a directory named after its recipe, hashed, and reused; a manifest
//! mismatch regenerates rather than silently scoring against different data.
//!
//! The generator is `tpchgen`, a Rust port of `dbgen` that reproduces the
//! reference generator's output. TPC-H's RNG is seeded by the algorithm itself,
//! so scale factor plus part count fixes the data completely — there is no
//! separate seed to pin.

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{BufReader, Read, Write};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use datafusion::parquet::arrow::ArrowWriter;
use datafusion::parquet::basic::Compression;
use datafusion::parquet::file::properties::WriterProperties;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};
use tpchgen::generators::{
    CustomerGenerator, LineItemGenerator, NationGenerator, OrderGenerator, PartGenerator,
    PartSuppGenerator, RegionGenerator, SupplierGenerator,
};
use tpchgen_arrow::{
    CustomerArrow, LineItemArrow, NationArrow, OrderArrow, PartArrow, PartSuppArrow, RecordBatchIterator,
    RegionArrow, SupplierArrow,
};

/// Bumped whenever anything about generation changes — the generator version,
/// the writer properties, the set of tables. An existing dataset with an older
/// recipe is regenerated instead of being trusted.
const RECIPE: &str = "tpchgen-2.0.2/tpchgen-arrow-2.0.1/snappy/8192";

const COMPRESSION: Compression = Compression::SNAPPY;
const BATCH_SIZE: usize = 8192;

pub const TABLES: [&str; 8] = [
    "customer", "lineitem", "nation", "orders", "part", "partsupp", "region", "supplier",
];

pub struct Dataset {
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    pub scale_factor: f64,
    /// sha256 over the per-file digests, in table order. This is the identifier
    /// a scored run records: it pins the data without shipping it.
    pub digest: String,
    pub rows: Vec<(String, u64)>,
}

impl Dataset {
    pub fn table_path(&self, table: &str) -> PathBuf {
        self.dir.join(format!("{table}.parquet"))
    }
}

/// Generate the dataset if it is not already present and intact.
pub fn materialise(root: &Path, scale_factor: f64) -> Result<Dataset, String> {
    let dir = root.join(format!("sf{}", format_scale(scale_factor)));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", dir.display()))?;

    if let Some(dataset) = reuse(&dir, scale_factor)? {
        return Ok(dataset);
    }

    eprintln!("generating TPC-H sf{} into {}", format_scale(scale_factor), dir.display());
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut digests = Vec::new();
    for table in TABLES {
        let path = dir.join(format!("{table}.parquet"));
        let count = generate(table, scale_factor, &path)?;
        let digest = sha256_file(&path)?;
        eprintln!("  {table:<9} {count:>9} rows  {}", &digest[..16]);
        rows.push((table.to_string(), count));
        digests.push((table.to_string(), digest));
    }

    let digest = combine(&digests);
    let manifest = Manifest {
        recipe: RECIPE.to_string(),
        scale_factor,
        digest: digest.clone(),
        files: digests,
        rows: rows.clone(),
    };
    let text = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&manifest).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let manifest_path = dir.join("MANIFEST.json");
    let mut f = File::create(&manifest_path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", manifest_path.display()))?;
    writeln!(f, "{text}").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;

    Ok(Dataset { dir, scale_factor, digest, rows })
}

#[derive(serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
struct Manifest {
    recipe: String,
    scale_factor: f64,
    digest: String,
    files: Vec<(String, String)>,
    rows: Vec<(String, u64)>,
}

/// Reuse an existing dataset only if every file still hashes to what the
/// manifest recorded. A half-written Parquet file from an interrupted run is
/// the failure this catches, and it would otherwise show up as a differential
/// mismatch blamed on the bridge.
fn reuse(dir: &Path, scale_factor: f64) -> Result<Option<Dataset>, String> {
    let manifest_path = dir.join("MANIFEST.json");
    let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let Ok(manifest) = serde_json::from_str::<Manifest>(&text) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    if manifest.recipe != RECIPE || manifest.scale_factor != scale_factor {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    for (table, expected) in &manifest.files {
        let path = dir.join(format!("{table}.parquet"));
        match sha256_file(&path) {
            Ok(actual) if &actual == expected => {}
            _ => {
                eprintln!("dataset at {} is stale or incomplete; regenerating", dir.display());
                return Ok(None);
            }
        }
    }
    eprintln!("reusing TPC-H sf{} at {} ({})", format_scale(scale_factor), dir.display(), &manifest.digest[..16]);
    Ok(Some(Dataset {
        dir: dir.to_path_buf(),
        scale_factor,
        digest: manifest.digest,
        rows: manifest.rows,
    }))
}

fn generate(table: &str, sf: f64, path: &Path) -> Result<u64, String> {
    // One part of one: a single file per table keeps the row-group layout, and
    // therefore DataFusion's partitioning, identical for both arms.
    match table {
        "customer" => write(path, CustomerArrow::new(CustomerGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "lineitem" => write(path, LineItemArrow::new(LineItemGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "nation" => write(path, NationArrow::new(NationGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "orders" => write(path, OrderArrow::new(OrderGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "part" => write(path, PartArrow::new(PartGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "partsupp" => write(path, PartSuppArrow::new(PartSuppGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "region" => write(path, RegionArrow::new(RegionGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        "supplier" => write(path, SupplierArrow::new(SupplierGenerator::new(sf, 1, 1)).with_batch_size(BATCH_SIZE)),
        other => Err(format!("no generator for table {other}")),
    }
}

fn write(path: &Path, mut batches: impl RecordBatchIterator) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let file = File::create(path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    let props = WriterProperties::builder().set_compression(COMPRESSION).build();
    let mut writer = ArrowWriter::try_new(file, batches.schema().clone(), Some(props))
        .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    let mut rows = 0u64;
    for batch in &mut batches {
        rows += batch.num_rows() as u64;
        writer.write(&batch).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    }
    writer.close().map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(rows)
}

fn sha256_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String, String> {
    let file = File::open(path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
    let mut reader = BufReader::new(file);
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; 1 << 20];
    loop {
        let n = reader.read(&mut buf).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        hasher.update(&buf[..n]);
    }
    Ok(hex(&hasher.finalize()))
}

fn combine(digests: &[(String, String)]) -> String {
    let mut hasher = Sha256::new();
    for (name, digest) in digests {
        hasher.update(name.as_bytes());
        hasher.update(b" ");
        hasher.update(digest.as_bytes());
        hasher.update(b"\n");
    }
    hex(&hasher.finalize())
}

fn hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    bytes.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// `sf1`, `sf10`, `sf0.1` — a directory name that survives a decimal scale.
pub fn format_scale(sf: f64) -> String {
    if sf.fract() == 0.0 {
        format!("{}", sf as u64)
    } else {
        format!("{sf}")
    }
}
//! Result-set comparison, as bags.
//!
//! This is the only check in the whole project that exercises
//! `crates/df-bridge`. No Lean theorem reaches `lower`/`lift`, so a bug there
//! is invisible to the proof pipeline and shows up only as a wrong answer on
//! real data. That is why it gates the run instead of annotating it: timings
//! taken against a wrong answer are worse than no timings, because they look
//! like a result.
//!
//! Comparison is as bags, not as sequences, because bag equivalence is exactly
//! what `Slot.Equiv` states and therefore exactly what the miner proved. A
//! query with `ORDER BY` does have a defined order, but the rule is never
//! allowed to lower the `Sort` node, so comparing sets of rows keeps the check
//! aligned with the guarantee rather than accidentally testing something
//! stronger that DataFusion, not the miner, is responsible for.

use datafusion::arrow::array::RecordBatch;
use datafusion::arrow::util::display::{ArrayFormatter, FormatOptions};

pub struct Mismatch {
    pub reason: String,
    /// Rows in the champion's answer that the challenger did not produce, and
    /// vice versa, capped so a wholly wrong answer does not print a database.
    pub only_champion: Vec<String>,
    pub only_challenger: Vec<String>,
}

const EXAMPLES: usize = 5;

pub fn compare(champion: &[RecordBatch], challenger: &[RecordBatch]) -> Result<(), Mismatch> {
    let champion_schema = schema_of(champion);
    let challenger_schema = schema_of(challenger);
    if champion_schema != challenger_schema {
        return Err(Mismatch {
            reason: format!(
                "schemas differ\n  champion:   {champion_schema}\n  challenger: {challenger_schema}"
            ),
            only_champion: Vec::new(),
            only_challenger: Vec::new(),
        });
    }

    let mut left = match rows(champion) {
        Ok(rows) => rows,
        Err(e) => return Err(plain(format!("formatting the champion's rows: {e}"))),
    };
    let mut right = match rows(challenger) {
        Ok(rows) => rows,
        Err(e) => return Err(plain(format!("formatting the challenger's rows: {e}"))),
    };

    left.sort_unstable();
    right.sort_unstable();
    if left == right {
        return Ok(());
    }

    // Multiset difference in both directions. Sorted, so one pass suffices, and
    // duplicates are handled by construction — a row produced twice on one side
    // and once on the other is a real mismatch under bag semantics.
    let mut only_champion = Vec::new();
    let mut only_challenger = Vec::new();
    let (mut i, mut j) = (0, 0);
    while i < left.len() && j < right.len() {
        match left[i].cmp(&right[j]) {
            std::cmp::Ordering::Equal => {
                i += 1;
                j += 1;
            }
            std::cmp::Ordering::Less => {
                push(&mut only_champion, &left[i]);
                i += 1;
            }
            std::cmp::Ordering::Greater => {
                push(&mut only_challenger, &right[j]);
                j += 1;
            }
        }
    }
    while i < left.len() {
        push(&mut only_champion, &left[i]);
        i += 1;
    }
    while j < right.len() {
        push(&mut only_challenger, &right[j]);
        j += 1;
    }

    Err(Mismatch {
        reason: format!(
            "result sets differ as bags: {} champion rows, {} challenger rows",
            left.len(),
            right.len()
        ),
        only_champion,
        only_challenger,
    })
}

fn push(into: &mut Vec<String>, row: &str) {
    if into.len() < EXAMPLES {
        into.push(row.replace('\u{1}', " | "));
    }
}

fn plain(reason: String) -> Mismatch {
    Mismatch { reason, only_champion: Vec::new(), only_challenger: Vec::new() }
}

fn schema_of(batches: &[RecordBatch]) -> String {
    match batches.first() {
        None => "<no batches>".to_string(),
        Some(batch) => batch
            .schema()
            .fields()
            .iter()
            .map(|f| format!("{}:{}", f.name(), f.data_type()))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(", "),
    }
}

/// Render every row to a canonical string. `\u{1}` separates columns because it
/// cannot occur in Arrow's own display output, so a value containing a comma or
/// a pipe cannot forge a column boundary and make two different rows compare
/// equal.
fn rows(batches: &[RecordBatch]) -> Result<Vec<String>, datafusion::arrow::error::ArrowError> {
    let options = FormatOptions::default().with_null("NULL");
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    for batch in batches {
        let formatters = batch
            .columns()
            .iter()
            .map(|column| ArrayFormatter::try_new(column, &options))
            .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
        for row in 0..batch.num_rows() {
            let mut rendered = String::new();
            for (i, formatter) in formatters.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    rendered.push('\u{1}');
                }
                rendered.push_str(&formatter.value(row).to_string());
            }
            out.push(rendered);
        }
    }
    Ok(out)
}
//! Two-arm benchmark and differential correctness harness.
//!
//! The first thing in this project that produces a number, and the number
//! answers the question the design rests on: can a rule expressible in the v1
//! fragment move TPC-H at all?
//!
//! Structure of a run, in the order the checks matter:
//!
//! 1. **Plan diagnostics.** Optimize every query on both arms and record
//!    whether the challenger's plan differs at all. A run where it never does
//!    has measured nothing, and the most common cause is a `LEAN_PATH` whose
//!    baseline `SlotEntry.olean` shadows the miner's — which turns the rule
//!    into the identity silently. This is reported before any timing so a
//!    1.000x geomean is never mistaken for a fair fight.
//! 2. **Differential check.** Every query on both arms, result sets compared as
//!    bags. `crates/df-bridge` is reached by no proof, so this is the only
//!    check that exercises it, and it gates the run rather than annotating it.
//! 3. **Timing.** Interleaved arms, the slot's repetition count, one discarded
//!    warm-up, trimmed median, geomean across queries.
//! 4. **Verdict.** Gates 2–6 of `docs/SCORING.md`.
//!
//! ```text
//! slot-bench [options] -- lean --run lean/Main.lean
//! ```
//!
//! The trailing argv is the rule host invocation, already wrapped in whatever
//! sandbox the caller wants. This crate deliberately has no opinion about the
//! sandbox: the local `just bench` and the validator impose different policies
//! and neither should have to fight the other's default.

mod arm;
mod data;
mod differential;
mod measure;
mod report;
mod selfcheck;
mod slot;

use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;
use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;
use std::time::Duration;

use arm::{Arm, ArmOptions, RulePosition};
use report::{BenchReport, Gates, Outcome, QueryReport, StatsReport};

const USAGE: &str = "\
slot-bench — two-arm benchmark and differential check

usage: slot-bench [options] -- <host-argv>...

  <host-argv>              the rule host, already sandboxed, e.g.
                           `lean --run lean/Main.lean`

  --slot <dir>             slot definition directory
                           [tasks/datafusion-logical-rewrite-v1]
  --data-dir <dir>         where the Parquet dataset lives [.work/tpch]
  --queries <dir>          directory of q<n>.sql [crates/bench/queries/tpch]
  --only <q1,q6,...>       run a subset of the slot's query set
  --scale <f64>            override the slot's scale factor
  --reps <n>               override the slot's repetition count
  --fuel <n>               override the slot's rewrite fuel
  --rule-position <p>      append | prepend [append]
  --disable-df-rule <name> disable a DataFusion optimizer rule in BOTH arms;
                           repeatable
  --target-partitions <n>  [available parallelism]
  --plan-time-budget-ms <n>  [250]
  --max-cv <fraction>      variance gate on either arm [0.05]
  --plans <dir>            where to write optimized plans [.work/bench/plans]
  --check-only             differential check only, no timing
  --self-check             positive control for the bridge: build plans in the
                           shapes the rule rewrites, execute them with
                           DataFusion's own rules off, and require the rewrite
                           counter to move. Runs before everything else.
  --json <path>            write the report as JSON
  -h, --help               this text

exit status: 0 promote · 1 reject · 2 void · 3 differential mismatch
             4 setup or usage error
";

struct Options {
    slot_dir: PathBuf,
    data_dir: PathBuf,
    queries_dir: PathBuf,
    only: Option<Vec<String>>,
    scale: Option<f64>,
    reps: Option<usize>,
    fuel: Option<u32>,
    position: RulePosition,
    disabled_df_rules: Vec<String>,
    target_partitions: usize,
    plan_time_budget: Duration,
    max_cv: f64,
    plans_dir: PathBuf,
    check_only: bool,
    self_check: bool,
    json: Option<PathBuf>,
    host: Vec<String>,
}

fn parse_args() -> Result<Options, String> {
    let mut options = Options {
        slot_dir: PathBuf::from("tasks/datafusion-logical-rewrite-v1"),
        data_dir: PathBuf::from(".work/tpch"),
        queries_dir: PathBuf::from("crates/bench/queries/tpch"),
        only: None,
        scale: None,
        reps: None,
        fuel: None,
        position: RulePosition::Append,
        disabled_df_rules: Vec::new(),
        target_partitions: std::thread::available_parallelism().map(|n| n.get()).unwrap_or(4),
        plan_time_budget: Duration::from_millis(250),
        max_cv: 0.05,
        plans_dir: PathBuf::from(".work/bench/plans"),
        check_only: false,
        self_check: false,
        json: None,
        host: Vec::new(),
    };

    let mut args = std::env::args().skip(1).peekable();
    while let Some(arg) = args.next() {
        let mut value = || args.next().ok_or_else(|| format!("{arg} needs a value"));
        match arg.as_str() {
            "--" => {
                options.host = args.collect();
                break;
            }
            "-h" | "--help" => {
                print!("{USAGE}");
                std::process::exit(0);
            }
            "--slot" => options.slot_dir = PathBuf::from(value()?),
            "--data-dir" => options.data_dir = PathBuf::from(value()?),
            "--queries" => options.queries_dir = PathBuf::from(value()?),
            "--only" => {
                options.only =
                    Some(value()?.split(',').map(|s| s.trim().to_string()).collect())
            }
            "--scale" => options.scale = Some(value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--scale: {e}"))?),
            "--reps" => options.reps = Some(value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--reps: {e}"))?),
            "--fuel" => options.fuel = Some(value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--fuel: {e}"))?),
            "--rule-position" => options.position = RulePosition::parse(&value()?)?,
            "--disable-df-rule" => options.disabled_df_rules.push(value()?),
            "--target-partitions" => {
                options.target_partitions =
                    value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--target-partitions: {e}"))?
            }
            "--plan-time-budget-ms" => {
                let ms: u64 = value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--plan-time-budget-ms: {e}"))?;
                options.plan_time_budget = Duration::from_millis(ms);
            }
            "--max-cv" => options.max_cv = value()?.parse().map_err(|e| format!("--max-cv: {e}"))?,
            "--plans" => options.plans_dir = PathBuf::from(value()?),
            "--check-only" => options.check_only = true,
            "--self-check" => options.self_check = true,
            "--json" => options.json = Some(PathBuf::from(value()?)),
            other => return Err(format!("unknown option {other:?}\n\n{USAGE}")),
        }
    }

    if options.host.is_empty() {
        return Err(format!(
            "no rule host given; the challenger arm needs one\n\n{USAGE}"
        ));
    }
    Ok(options)
}

fn main() {
    let options = match parse_args() {
        Ok(options) => options,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: {e}");
            std::process::exit(4);
        }
    };

    // A multi-thread runtime, because DataFusion's execution is the thing being
    // measured and a current-thread runtime would measure a serialised version
    // of it.
    let runtime = match tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().enable_all().build() {
        Ok(runtime) => runtime,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: building the tokio runtime: {e}");
            std::process::exit(4);
        }
    };

    let code = runtime.block_on(run(options));
    std::process::exit(code);
}

async fn run(options: Options) -> i32 {
    let slot = match slot::Slot::load(&options.slot_dir) {
        Ok(slot) => slot,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: {e}");
            return 4;
        }
    };

    let scale = options.scale.unwrap_or(slot.workloads.public.scale_factor);
    let reps = options.reps.unwrap_or(slot.scoring.repetitions);
    let fuel = options.fuel.unwrap_or(slot.artifact.fuel);
    if reps < 2 {
        eprintln!("slot-bench: --reps must be at least 2; the first is a discarded warm-up");
        return 4;
    }

    let queries = match load_queries(&options, &slot) {
        Ok(queries) => queries,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: {e}");
            return 4;
        }
    };

    let dataset = match data::materialise(&options.data_dir, scale) {
        Ok(dataset) => dataset,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: {e}");
            return 4;
        }
    };

    eprintln!(
        "dataset {} sf{} — {}",
        &dataset.digest[..16],
        data::format_scale(dataset.scale_factor),
        dataset
            .rows
            .iter()
            .map(|(table, rows)| format!("{table} {rows}"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join(", ")
    );

    let arm_options = ArmOptions {
        target_partitions: options.target_partitions,
        disabled_df_rules: &options.disabled_df_rules,
        position: options.position,
        fuel,
        rewrite_timeout: Duration::from_millis(slot.artifact.rewrite_timeout_ms),
    };

    let champion = match arm::build("champion", &dataset, &arm_options, None).await {
        Ok(arm) => arm,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("slot-bench: champion arm: {e}");
            return 4;
        }
    };
    let challenger =
        match arm::build("challenger", &dataset, &arm_options, Some(host_command(&options.host)))
            .await
        {
            Ok(arm) => arm,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: challenger arm: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };

    if options.self_check {
        let cases = match selfcheck::run(&dataset, &arm_options, &options.host).await {
            Ok(cases) => cases,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: self-check: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };
        println!(
            "\nbridge self-check — lower, host, rule, lift, execute\n\
             (DataFusion's own logical rules are off in both control arms, so nothing else\n\
              can reach these shapes first)\n"
        );
        println!(
            "{:<16} {:<24} {:>8} {:>4} {:>5} {:>5} {:>4} {:>5} {:>3}  {}",
            "case", "plan shape", "rows", "rw", "decl", "unch", "err", "lift", "wv", "answers"
        );
        let mut failed = 0;
        for case in &cases {
            println!(
                "{:<16} {:<24} {:>8} {:>4} {:>5} {:>5} {:>4} {:>5} {:>3}  {}",
                case.name,
                case.shape,
                case.rows,
                case.rewrites,
                case.declined,
                case.unchanged,
                case.errors,
                case.lift_failures,
                case.width_violations,
                if case.agreed { "agree" } else { "DISAGREE" }
            );
            if !case.agreed {
                failed += 1;
            }
        }
        if failed > 0 {
            eprintln!("\n{failed} self-check cases disagree: crates/df-bridge is wrong.");
            return 3;
        }
        // A rule that does not match the control shapes is not a broken bridge, and
        // conflating the two made this check fail on the first submission that was
        // not the reference rule. What proves the round trip is healthy is that the
        // host *answered*: `unchanged` counts a plan that went out over the wire,
        // came back, and compared equal, which exercises lower, the codec and the
        // host. Only the rewrite path is left unexercised, and that is a warning.
        let answered: u64 = cases.iter().map(|c| c.rewrites + c.unchanged).sum();
        let protocol_errors: u64 = cases.iter().map(|c| c.errors).sum();
        if answered == 0 || protocol_errors > 0 {
            eprintln!(
                "\nthe host did not answer: {answered} plans round-tripped and {protocol_errors} \
                 failed at the protocol. The bridge round trip is not working, or the host is not \
                 running — check the LEAN_PATH ordering, which silently substitutes the baseline \
                 rule when the entry directory does not come first."
            );
            return 3;
        }
        if cases.iter().all(|c| c.rewrites == 0) {
            eprintln!(
                "\nnote: the rule declined all {} control shapes, so the round trip is proved only \
                 for the decline path ({answered} plans went out and came back). That is expected \
                 for a rule that does not target filter/projection shapes; it is not evidence of a \
                 bridge problem.",
                cases.len()
            );
        }
        println!();
    }

    // ---- phase 1: plan diagnostics -------------------------------------------
    //
    // Before anything is timed, establish whether the rule has any effect on
    // the plan. This is cheap and it is the difference between "no speedup" and
    // "no experiment".
    let mut plan_changed = Vec::new();
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::create_dir_all(&options.plans_dir) {
        eprintln!("slot-bench: {}: {e}", options.plans_dir.display());
        return 4;
    }
    for (name, sql) in &queries {
        let champion_plan = match measure::optimized_plan(&champion, sql).await {
            Ok(text) => text,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the champion: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };
        let challenger_plan = match measure::optimized_plan(&challenger, sql).await {
            Ok(text) => text,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the challenger: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };
        write_plan(&options.plans_dir, name, "champion", &champion_plan);
        write_plan(&options.plans_dir, name, "challenger", &challenger_plan);
        plan_changed.push(champion_plan != challenger_plan);
    }

    // The diagnostics above went through the host too. Zero the counters so the
    // reported stats describe the scored work and nothing else.
    if let Some(stats) = &challenger.stats {
        stats.attempts.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.rewrites.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.declined.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.unchanged.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.errors.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.lift_failures.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        stats.host_micros.store(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        // width_violations is deliberately not zeroed: one anywhere, at any
        // point in the process, is enough to void the run.
    }

    // ---- phase 2: differential check -----------------------------------------
    let mut rows = Vec::new();
    let mut per_query_rewrites = Vec::new();
    let mut per_query_declined = Vec::new();
    let mut mismatches = 0;
    for (name, sql) in &queries {
        let before = snapshot(&challenger);
        let champion_run = match measure::run(&champion, sql).await {
            Ok(run) => run,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the champion: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };
        let challenger_run = match measure::run(&challenger, sql).await {
            Ok(run) => run,
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the challenger: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        };
        let after = snapshot(&challenger);
        per_query_rewrites.push(after.0 - before.0);
        per_query_declined.push(after.1 - before.1);
        rows.push(champion_run.batches.iter().map(|b| b.num_rows()).sum::<usize>());

        match differential::compare(&champion_run.batches, &challenger_run.batches) {
            Ok(()) => {}
            Err(mismatch) => {
                mismatches += 1;
                eprintln!("\nDIFFERENTIAL MISMATCH on {name}: {}", mismatch.reason);
                for row in &mismatch.only_champion {
                    eprintln!("  champion only:   {row}");
                }
                for row in &mismatch.only_challenger {
                    eprintln!("  challenger only: {row}");
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if mismatches > 0 {
        eprintln!(
            "\n{mismatches} of {} queries disagree. This is a bug in crates/df-bridge, not in the \
             Lean: no proof reaches lower/lift. Timing is not run — numbers taken against a wrong \
             answer look like a result and are not one.",
            queries.len()
        );
        return 3;
    }
    eprintln!("differential check: {} queries agree as bags", queries.len());

    if options.check_only {
        return 0;
    }

    // ---- phase 3: timing ------------------------------------------------------
    let mut champion_exec: Vec<Vec<Duration>> = vec![Vec::new(); queries.len()];
    let mut challenger_exec: Vec<Vec<Duration>> = vec![Vec::new(); queries.len()];
    let mut champion_plan: Vec<Vec<Duration>> = vec![Vec::new(); queries.len()];
    let mut challenger_plan: Vec<Vec<Duration>> = vec![Vec::new(); queries.len()];

    for rep in 0..reps {
        // Alternate which arm goes first. Interleaving alone still gives the
        // second arm a warmer cache within each pair; alternating cancels it.
        let champion_first = rep % 2 == 0;
        for (index, (name, sql)) in queries.iter().enumerate() {
            let (a, b) = if champion_first {
                (&champion, &challenger)
            } else {
                (&challenger, &champion)
            };
            let first = match measure::run(a, sql).await {
                Ok(run) => run,
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the {}: {e}", a.name);
                    return 4;
                }
            };
            let second = match measure::run(b, sql).await {
                Ok(run) => run,
                Err(e) => {
                    eprintln!("slot-bench: {name} on the {}: {e}", b.name);
                    return 4;
                }
            };
            if rep == 0 {
                continue; // warm-up
            }
            let (champ, chall) = if champion_first { (first, second) } else { (second, first) };
            champion_exec[index].push(champ.exec);
            challenger_exec[index].push(chall.exec);
            champion_plan[index].push(champ.plan);
            challenger_plan[index].push(chall.plan);
        }
        eprintln!("rep {}/{} done", rep + 1, reps);
    }

    // ---- phase 4: report ------------------------------------------------------
    let mut query_reports = Vec::new();
    for (index, (name, _)) in queries.iter().enumerate() {
        let champion_ms = measure::trimmed_median(&champion_exec[index]).as_secs_f64() * 1000.0;
        let challenger_ms = measure::trimmed_median(&challenger_exec[index]).as_secs_f64() * 1000.0;
        query_reports.push(QueryReport {
            name: name.clone(),
            rows: rows[index],
            plan_changed: plan_changed[index],
            rewrites: per_query_rewrites[index],
            declined: per_query_declined[index],
            champion_exec_ms: champion_ms,
            challenger_exec_ms: challenger_ms,
            speedup: if challenger_ms > 0.0 { champion_ms / challenger_ms } else { 1.0 },
            champion_plan_ms: measure::trimmed_median(&champion_plan[index]).as_secs_f64() * 1000.0,
            challenger_plan_ms: measure::trimmed_median(&challenger_plan[index]).as_secs_f64()
                * 1000.0,
            champion_cv: measure::coefficient_of_variation(&champion_exec[index]),
            challenger_cv: measure::coefficient_of_variation(&challenger_exec[index]),
        });
    }

    let stats = stats_report(&challenger);
    let gates = Gates {
        min_improvement: slot.scoring.min_improvement,
        max_single_query_regression: slot.scoring.max_single_query_regression,
        plan_time_budget: options.plan_time_budget,
        max_cv: options.max_cv,
    };
    let verdict = report::verdict(&query_reports, &stats, &gates);
    let speedups: Vec<f64> = query_reports.iter().map(|q| q.speedup).collect();
    let report = BenchReport {
        slot_id: slot.slot_id,
        engine: format!("{} {}", slot.engine.name, slot.engine.version),
        scale_factor: scale,
        dataset_digest: dataset.digest,
        repetitions: reps,
        scored_repetitions: reps - 1,
        target_partitions: options.target_partitions,
        rule_position: format!("{:?}", options.position).to_lowercase(),
        disabled_df_rules: options.disabled_df_rules.clone(),
        geomean_speedup: measure::geomean(&speedups),
        worst_regression: speedups.iter().map(|s| 1.0 - s).fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max),
        plan_time_budget_ms: options.plan_time_budget.as_secs_f64() * 1000.0,
        queries: query_reports,
        stats,
        verdict,
    };

    println!("\n{}", report.render());

    if let Some(path) = &options.json {
        match serde_json::to_string_pretty(&report) {
            Ok(text) => {
                if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(path, text + "\n") {
                    eprintln!("slot-bench: {}: {e}", path.display());
                    return 4;
                }
            }
            Err(e) => {
                eprintln!("slot-bench: serialising the report: {e}");
                return 4;
            }
        }
    }

    match report.verdict.outcome {
        Outcome::Promote => 0,
        Outcome::Reject => 1,
        Outcome::Void => 2,
    }
}

fn host_command(argv: &[String]) -> Command {
    let mut command = Command::new(&argv[0]);
    command.args(&argv[1..]);
    command
}

fn snapshot(arm: &Arm) -> (u64, u64) {
    match &arm.stats {
        None => (0, 0),
        Some(stats) => (
            stats.rewrites.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            stats.declined.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        ),
    }
}

fn stats_report(arm: &Arm) -> StatsReport {
    match &arm.stats {
        None => StatsReport::default(),
        Some(stats) => StatsReport {
            attempts: stats.attempts.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            rewrites: stats.rewrites.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            declined: stats.declined.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            unchanged: stats.unchanged.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            errors: stats.errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            lift_failures: stats.lift_failures.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            width_violations: stats.width_violations.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            host_millis: stats.host_micros.load(Ordering::Relaxed) as f64 / 1000.0,
        },
    }
}
