fn load_queries(options: &Options, slot: &slot::Slot) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>, String> {
    // `--only` names files directly rather than filtering the slot's list, so a
    // miner can point `--queries` at their own directory without having to
    // number it the way the public set is numbered.
    let names: Vec<String> = match &options.only {
        Some(only) => only.clone(),
        None => slot.workloads.public.queries.iter().map(|n| format!("q{n}")).collect(),
    };
    let mut queries = Vec::new();
    for name in names {
        let path = options.queries_dir.join(format!("{name}.sql"));
        let sql = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        queries.push((name, sql));
    }
    if queries.is_empty() {
        return Err("no queries selected".to_string());
    }
    Ok(queries)
}

fn write_plan(dir: &Path, query: &str, arm: &str, text: &str) {
    let path = dir.join(format!("{query}.{arm}.txt"));
    if let Err(e) = std::fs::write(&path, text) {
        eprintln!("slot-bench: {}: {e}", path.display());
    }
}
//! Running a query, and turning repetitions into one number.
//!
//! The protocol is `docs/SCORING.md`'s, and the reasons are the usual ones:
//! interleaving the arms rather than running them in blocks means thermal drift
//! and background load hit both; discarding a warm-up keeps page-cache warming
//! out of the measurement; a trimmed median rather than a mean means one
//! scheduler hiccup does not decide the run.

use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use datafusion::arrow::array::RecordBatch;
use datafusion::physical_plan::collect;

use crate::arm::Arm;

pub struct Run {
    /// Analyzer, logical optimizer (including every Lean round trip) and
    /// physical planning. Scored against the plan-time budget.
    pub plan: Duration,
    /// Execution only. This is the number the ladder is about.
    pub exec: Duration,
    pub batches: Vec<RecordBatch>,
}

pub async fn run(arm: &Arm, sql: &str) -> Result<Run, String> {
    // Parsing is outside the timers: it is identical for both arms and belongs
    // to neither planning nor execution.
    let frame = arm.ctx.sql(sql).await.map_err(|e| format!("planning: {e}"))?;

    let started = Instant::now();
    let physical = frame.create_physical_plan().await.map_err(|e| format!("optimizing: {e}"))?;
    let plan = started.elapsed();

    let started = Instant::now();
    let batches =
        collect(physical, arm.ctx.task_ctx()).await.map_err(|e| format!("executing: {e}"))?;
    let exec = started.elapsed();

    Ok(Run { plan, exec, batches })
}

/// The optimized logical plan as text, for the report. Cheap, and the only way
/// to tell "the rule fired and the plan is genuinely different" from "the rule
/// fired and DataFusion undid it on the next pass".
pub async fn optimized_plan(arm: &Arm, sql: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    let state = arm.ctx.state();
    let plan = state.create_logical_plan(sql).await.map_err(|e| format!("planning: {e}"))?;
    let optimized = state.optimize(&plan).map_err(|e| format!("optimizing: {e}"))?;
    Ok(format!("{}", optimized.display_indent_schema()))
}

/// Drop the lowest and highest sample, then take the median of what is left.
///
/// With the slot's 7 repetitions the first is discarded as a warm-up, leaving
/// 6; trimming leaves 4 and the result is the mean of the middle two. Panics on
/// an empty slice: a query with no samples is a bug in the caller, not a
/// measurement worth reporting.
pub fn trimmed_median(samples: &[Duration]) -> Duration {
    assert!(!samples.is_empty(), "trimmed_median of no samples");
    let mut sorted: Vec<u128> = samples.iter().map(|d| d.as_nanos()).collect();
    sorted.sort_unstable();
    let slice: &[u128] = if sorted.len() >= 4 { &sorted[1..sorted.len() - 1] } else { &sorted };
    let mid = slice.len() / 2;
    let nanos = if slice.len() % 2 == 0 {
        (slice[mid - 1] + slice[mid]) / 2
    } else {
        slice[mid]
    };
    Duration::from_nanos(nanos as u64)
}

/// Coefficient of variation of the samples, as a fraction. A run whose arms are
/// noisier than the improvement they claim is not evidence of anything.
pub fn coefficient_of_variation(samples: &[Duration]) -> f64 {
    if samples.len() < 2 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let values: Vec<f64> = samples.iter().map(|d| d.as_secs_f64()).collect();
    let mean = values.iter().sum::<f64>() / values.len() as f64;
    if mean == 0.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let variance =
        values.iter().map(|v| (v - mean).powi(2)).sum::<f64>() / (values.len() - 1) as f64;
    variance.sqrt() / mean
}

/// Geometric mean of per-query speedups. Geometric because a speedup is a
/// ratio: the arithmetic mean of ratios is dominated by whichever query happens
/// to be fastest, which is the opposite of what the ladder wants to reward.
pub fn geomean(speedups: &[f64]) -> f64 {
    if speedups.is_empty() {
        return 1.0;
    }
    let sum: f64 = speedups.iter().map(|s| s.ln()).sum();
    (sum / speedups.len() as f64).exp()
}
//! The report, and the verdict derived from it.
//!
//! The verdict implements gates 2–6 of `docs/SCORING.md`. Gate 1 — the Lean
//! pipeline accepted the submission — is not this crate's business and is
//! assumed by the fact that a run happened at all.
//!
//! `width_violations` deserves its own sentence. `Slot.Sound` proves that a
//! rewrite preserves width, so a non-zero count does not mean "the rule is
//! bad", it means the process on the other end of the pipe is not the program
//! that was proved: a packaging bug, a stale `.olean`, or tampering. The run is
//! **void**, and voiding is deliberately a different outcome from failing.

use std::time::Duration;

use serde::Serialize;

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct BenchReport {
    pub slot_id: String,
    pub engine: String,
    pub scale_factor: f64,
    pub dataset_digest: String,
    pub repetitions: usize,
    pub scored_repetitions: usize,
    pub target_partitions: usize,
    pub rule_position: String,
    pub disabled_df_rules: Vec<String>,
    pub queries: Vec<QueryReport>,
    pub geomean_speedup: f64,
    /// The largest single-query regression, as a fraction. Positive means some
    /// query got slower.
    pub worst_regression: f64,
    pub plan_time_budget_ms: f64,
    pub stats: StatsReport,
    pub verdict: Verdict,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct QueryReport {
    pub name: String,
    pub rows: usize,
    /// Whether the challenger's optimized logical plan differs from the
    /// champion's at all. A run where this is false everywhere has measured
    /// nothing, however good the geomean looks.
    pub plan_changed: bool,
    pub rewrites: u64,
    pub declined: u64,
    pub champion_exec_ms: f64,
    pub challenger_exec_ms: f64,
    pub speedup: f64,
    pub champion_plan_ms: f64,
    pub challenger_plan_ms: f64,
    pub champion_cv: f64,
    pub challenger_cv: f64,
}

#[derive(Serialize, Default)]
pub struct StatsReport {
    pub attempts: u64,
    pub rewrites: u64,
    pub declined: u64,
    pub unchanged: u64,
    pub errors: u64,
    pub lift_failures: u64,
    pub width_violations: u64,
    pub host_millis: f64,
}

#[derive(Serialize, PartialEq, Eq, Clone, Copy, Debug)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Outcome {
    /// Clears every gate.
    Promote,
    /// Correct, but not enough faster, or too slow somewhere.
    Reject,
    /// The run itself cannot be trusted. Not a statement about the submission.
    Void,
}

#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Verdict {
    pub outcome: Outcome,
    pub reasons: Vec<String>,
}

pub struct Gates {
    pub min_improvement: f64,
    pub max_single_query_regression: f64,
    pub plan_time_budget: Duration,
    pub max_cv: f64,
}

pub fn verdict(queries: &[QueryReport], stats: &StatsReport, gates: &Gates) -> Verdict {
    let mut reasons = Vec::new();

    if stats.width_violations > 0 {
        reasons.push(format!(
            "WIDTH_VIOLATION: {} rewrites changed the plan's width, which `Slot.Sound` proves \
             is impossible — the running artifact is not the proved rule",
            stats.width_violations
        ));
        return Verdict { outcome: Outcome::Void, reasons };
    }

    // Noise only invalidates a measurement when it could *explain* it. Voiding a
    // 181x win because a 5 ms query jittered by 20% is the gate misfiring: the
    // signal is three orders of magnitude clear of the noise. So a query counts as
    // unresolved only when it is both noisy and its effect sits inside the noise.
    //
    // `resolved` uses the sum of the two arms' coefficients of variation as a crude
    // combined uncertainty. Crude is fine here — it is used to decide whether an
    // effect is *obviously* clear of the noise, not to put an interval on it.
    let resolved = |q: &QueryReport| {
        (q.speedup - 1.0).abs() > q.champion_cv + q.challenger_cv
    };
    let noisy: Vec<&QueryReport> = queries
        .iter()
        .filter(|q| (q.champion_cv > gates.max_cv || q.challenger_cv > gates.max_cv)
                    && !resolved(q))
        .collect();
    if !noisy.is_empty() {
        reasons.push(format!(
            "BENCH_VARIANCE: {} of {} queries exceed cv {:.1}% with an effect inside the noise. \
             A run this noisy cannot resolve the {:.0}% bar the ladder is decided on, so it is \
             void rather than scored. `docs/SCORING.md` requires a pinned CPU governor, isolated \
             cores and no other tenant; a developer machine is none of those and wants --max-cv \
             loosened, not this gate ignored. ({})",
            noisy.len(),
            queries.len(),
            gates.max_cv * 100.0,
            gates.min_improvement * 100.0,
            noisy
                .iter()
                .map(|q| format!("{} {:.1}%/{:.1}%", q.name, q.champion_cv * 100.0, q.challenger_cv * 100.0))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        ));
        return Verdict { outcome: Outcome::Void, reasons };
    }

    let budget_ms = gates.plan_time_budget.as_secs_f64() * 1000.0;
    let over: Vec<&QueryReport> =
        queries.iter().filter(|q| q.challenger_plan_ms > budget_ms).collect();
    if !over.is_empty() {
        reasons.push(format!(
            "PLAN_TIME_EXCEEDED: {} over the {budget_ms:.0} ms budget ({})",
            over.len(),
            over.iter()
                .map(|q| format!("{} {:.0} ms", q.name, q.challenger_plan_ms))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        ));
    }

    // Same correction the other way round: an apparent regression that is inside
    // the measurement noise is not evidence of a regression. Without this, a query
    // whose two arms run *identical plans* fails the 1% cap whenever the machine
    // hiccups, which is what happens on every fast query.
    let regressed: Vec<&QueryReport> = queries
        .iter()
        .filter(|q| 1.0 - q.speedup > gates.max_single_query_regression && resolved(q))
        .collect();
    if !regressed.is_empty() {
        reasons.push(format!(
            "REGRESSION_CAP_EXCEEDED: {} regressed by more than {:.1}% ({})",
            regressed.len(),
            gates.max_single_query_regression * 100.0,
            regressed
                .iter()
                .map(|q| format!("{} {:.1}%", q.name, (1.0 - q.speedup) * 100.0))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(", ")
        ));
    }

    let speedups: Vec<f64> = queries.iter().map(|q| q.speedup).collect();
    let geomean = crate::measure::geomean(&speedups);
    if geomean < 1.0 + gates.min_improvement {
        reasons.push(format!(
            "NOT_FASTER: geomean {geomean:.4} below the {:.4} bar",
            1.0 + gates.min_improvement
        ));
    }

    if queries.iter().all(|q| !q.plan_changed) {
        let lowered = stats.attempts.saturating_sub(stats.declined);
        let diagnosis = if stats.attempts == 0 {
            "the rule was never invoked at all — check `apply_order`"
        } else if lowered == 0 {
            "the bridge declined every node, so the v1 fragment does not reach this workload; \
             `crates/df-bridge` is what to work on, not the rule"
        } else if stats.rewrites == 0 {
            "the bridge lowered nodes and the rule declined all of them; the fragment reaches \
             this workload but the rule finds nothing in it"
        } else {
            "the rule rewrote nodes and DataFusion undid the change on a later pass"
        };
        reasons.push(format!(
            "NO_EFFECT: the challenger's optimized plan is identical to the champion's on every \
             query — {diagnosis}. If none of that fits, check the LEAN_PATH ordering: a baseline \
             SlotEntry.olean ahead of the miner's turns the rule into the identity silently."
        ));
    }

    let outcome = if reasons.is_empty() { Outcome::Promote } else { Outcome::Reject };
    Verdict { outcome, reasons }
}

impl BenchReport {
    pub fn render(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        let p = &mut out;

        push(p, &format!("slot            {}", self.slot_id));
        push(p, &format!("engine          {}", self.engine));
        push(p, &format!("data            tpch sf{} {}", crate::data::format_scale(self.scale_factor), &self.dataset_digest[..16]));
        push(p, &format!("protocol        {} reps ({} scored), trimmed median, interleaved arms", self.repetitions, self.scored_repetitions));
        push(p, &format!("partitions      {}", self.target_partitions));
        push(p, &format!("rule position   {}", self.rule_position));
        if !self.disabled_df_rules.is_empty() {
            push(p, &format!("df rules off    {} (both arms)", self.disabled_df_rules.join(", ")));
        }
        push(p, "");

        push(
            p,
            "query        rows    plan?  rw   champion   challenger    speedup   plan ms (c/x)    cv (c/x)",
        );
        push(
            p,
            "---------- ------- ------- ---- ---------- ------------ --------- --------------- -------------",
        );
        for q in &self.queries {
            push(
                p,
                &format!(
                    "{:<10} {:>7} {:>7} {:>4} {:>8.1}ms {:>10.1}ms {:>8.3}x {:>6.1}/{:<8.1} {:>5}/{:<6}",
                    q.name,
                    q.rows,
                    if q.plan_changed { "changed" } else { "same" },
                    q.rewrites,
                    q.champion_exec_ms,
                    q.challenger_exec_ms,
                    q.speedup,
                    q.champion_plan_ms,
                    q.challenger_plan_ms,
                    format!("{:.1}%", q.champion_cv * 100.0),
                    format!("{:.1}%", q.challenger_cv * 100.0),
                ),
            );
        }
        push(p, "");
        push(p, &format!("geomean speedup      {:.4}x", self.geomean_speedup));
        push(
            p,
            &format!(
                "worst single query   {:+.2}%{}",
                -self.worst_regression * 100.0,
                if self.worst_regression <= 0.0 { " (nothing regressed)" } else { "" }
            ),
        );
        push(
            p,
            &format!(
                "rule stats           attempts {} · lowered {} · declined {} · rewritten {} · unchanged {} · errors {} · lift failures {} · width violations {}",
                self.stats.attempts,
                self.stats.attempts.saturating_sub(self.stats.declined),
                self.stats.declined,
                self.stats.rewrites,
                self.stats.unchanged,
                self.stats.errors,
                self.stats.lift_failures,
                self.stats.width_violations
            ),
        );
        push(p, &format!("host round trips     {:.1} ms total", self.stats.host_millis));
        push(p, "");
        push(p, &format!("verdict              {:?}", self.verdict.outcome));
        for reason in &self.verdict.reasons {
            push(p, &format!("  - {reason}"));
        }
        out
    }
}

fn push(out: &mut String, line: &str) {
    out.push_str(line);
    out.push('\n');
}
//! A positive control for the bridge.
//!
//! Everything else in this harness can report "the rule never fired" for two
//! completely different reasons: because the workload contains nothing the rule
//! matches, or because `lower`, the host, or `lift` is broken. Those look
//! identical in the counters and they call for opposite work, so one of them has
//! to be ruled out directly.
//!
//! This is that check. It builds plans in the shapes the reference submission
//! rewrites — a filter above a projection, two adjacent filters, a filter on
//! literal `TRUE` — using `LogicalPlanBuilder` rather than SQL, because SQL
//! cannot produce them: `WHERE` is planned below `SELECT`, so a filter is never
//! above a projection until an optimizer rule puts it there. Then it executes
//! them on both arms and requires the answers to agree and the rewrite counter
//! to move.
//!
//! Both control arms run with DataFusion's own logical rules switched **off** —
//! the control champion has an empty rule list and the control challenger has
//! only the miner's rule. Otherwise the check cannot tell a broken bridge from
//! `push_down_filter` having reached the shape first, which is the one
//! distinction it exists to make. It therefore says nothing about how the rule
//! fares in competition; that is what the scored run is for.
//!
//! It is the only test in the repository that exercises the whole
//! `lower → wire → Lean rule → wire → lift → execute` path against a real
//! DataFusion plan. Until it passes, every claim about `crates/df-bridge` is
//! unverified.

use std::sync::atomic::Ordering;

use datafusion::common::ScalarValue;
use datafusion::dataframe::DataFrame;
use datafusion::logical_expr::{col, lit, LogicalPlan, LogicalPlanBuilder};

use std::process::Command;

use crate::arm::{self, Arm, ArmOptions};
use crate::data::Dataset;
use crate::differential;

pub struct Case {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub shape: &'static str,
    pub rows: usize,
    pub rewrites: u64,
    /// The counters that say *why* a case did not rewrite. Without them a zero
    /// in the rewrites column has four possible causes -- the bridge declined,
    /// the rule declined, `lift` failed, or the width check fired -- and they
    /// call for completely different work.
    pub declined: u64,
    pub unchanged: u64,
    pub errors: u64,
    pub lift_failures: u64,
    pub width_violations: u64,
    pub agreed: bool,
}

/// `l_shipdate` is a `Date32`, so this also covers the literal round trip that
/// dates need: lowered to an epoch offset, and given its type back on the way
/// out. A predicate that survives `lower` but comes back as an `Int64` produces
/// a plan DataFusion refuses to type, and the rewrite is dropped silently.
fn shipdate_after(day: i32) -> datafusion::logical_expr::Expr {
    col("l_shipdate").gt(lit(ScalarValue::Date32(Some(day))))
}

pub async fn run(
    dataset: &Dataset,
    options: &ArmOptions<'_>,
    host: &[String],
) -> Result<Vec<Case>, String> {
    let champion = arm::build_isolated("control-champion", dataset, options, None).await?;
    let mut command = Command::new(&host[0]);
    command.args(&host[1..]);
    let challenger =
        arm::build_isolated("control-challenger", dataset, options, Some(command)).await?;
    let (champion, challenger) = (&champion, &challenger);

    let mut cases = Vec::new();

    // Filter above a projection: the rewrite with the actual value in it, since
    // the projection then runs on fewer rows.
    cases.push(
        case(champion, challenger, "filter/project", "Filter(Projection(Scan))", |builder| {
            builder
                .project(vec![col("l_orderkey"), col("l_shipdate")])?
                .filter(shipdate_after(9200))?
                .build()
        })
        .await?,
    );

    // Two adjacent filters: one predicate evaluated per row instead of two.
    cases.push(
        case(champion, challenger, "filter/filter", "Filter(Filter(Scan))", |builder| {
            builder
                .filter(shipdate_after(9200))?
                .filter(col("l_orderkey").lt(lit(1_000_000i64)))?
                .build()
        })
        .await?,
    );

    // A filter on literal TRUE. In a scored run DataFusion's own
    // `eliminate_filter` gets to this first; here nothing does, so the case is
    // as meaningful as the other two.
    cases.push(
        case(champion, challenger, "filter/true", "Filter(TRUE, Scan)", |builder| {
            builder.filter(lit(true))?.build()
        })
        .await?,
    );

    Ok(cases)
}

async fn case<F>(
    champion: &Arm,
    challenger: &Arm,
    name: &'static str,
    shape: &'static str,
    build: F,
) -> Result<Case, String>
where
    F: Fn(LogicalPlanBuilder) -> datafusion::error::Result<LogicalPlan>,
{
    let champion_plan = build(base(champion).await?).map_err(|e| format!("{name}: {e}"))?;
    let challenger_plan = build(base(challenger).await?).map_err(|e| format!("{name}: {e}"))?;

    let before = counter(challenger);
    let champion_rows = collect(champion, champion_plan).await.map_err(|e| format!("{name} on the champion: {e}"))?;
    let challenger_rows =
        collect(challenger, challenger_plan).await.map_err(|e| format!("{name} on the challenger: {e}"))?;
    let after = counter(challenger);

    let agreed = match differential::compare(&champion_rows, &challenger_rows) {
        Ok(()) => true,
        Err(mismatch) => {
            eprintln!("self-check {name}: {}", mismatch.reason);
            for row in mismatch.only_champion.iter().chain(mismatch.only_challenger.iter()) {
                eprintln!("  {row}");
            }
            false
        }
    };

    Ok(Case {
        name,
        shape,
        rows: champion_rows.iter().map(|b| b.num_rows()).sum(),
        rewrites: after.0 - before.0,
        declined: after.1 - before.1,
        unchanged: after.2 - before.2,
        errors: after.3 - before.3,
        lift_failures: after.4 - before.4,
        width_violations: after.5 - before.5,
        agreed,
    })
}

/// A `TableScan` of `lineitem`, unoptimized, as the root to build on.
async fn base(arm: &Arm) -> Result<LogicalPlanBuilder, String> {
    let table = arm.ctx.table("lineitem").await.map_err(|e| format!("reading lineitem: {e}"))?;
    Ok(LogicalPlanBuilder::from(table.into_unoptimized_plan()))
}

async fn collect(
    arm: &Arm,
    plan: LogicalPlan,
) -> datafusion::error::Result<Vec<datafusion::arrow::array::RecordBatch>> {
    DataFrame::new(arm.ctx.state(), plan).collect().await
}

/// (rewrites, declined, unchanged, errors, lift_failures, width_violations)
fn counter(arm: &Arm) -> (u64, u64, u64, u64, u64, u64) {
    match &arm.stats {
        None => (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0),
        Some(s) => (
            s.rewrites.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            s.declined.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            s.unchanged.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            s.errors.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            s.lift_failures.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
            s.width_violations.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        ),
    }
}
//! The parts of a slot definition the harness needs.
//!
//! `tasks/<slot>/slot.json` is the source of truth for scale factor, query set,
//! fuel, and every scoring constant. The harness reads them rather than
//! carrying its own defaults, because a benchmark run that disagrees with the
//! slot it claims to score is worse than no run at all: the numbers look
//! authoritative and mean nothing.

use std::path::Path;

use serde::Deserialize;

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Slot {
    pub slot_id: String,
    pub engine: Engine,
    pub artifact: Artifact,
    pub workloads: Workloads,
    pub scoring: Scoring,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Engine {
    pub name: String,
    pub version: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Artifact {
    pub fuel: u32,
    pub rewrite_timeout_ms: u64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Workloads {
    pub public: Workload,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Workload {
    pub kind: String,
    pub scale_factor: f64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub queries: Vec<u32>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Deserialize)]
pub struct Scoring {
    pub repetitions: usize,
    pub aggregate: String,
    pub min_improvement: f64,
    pub max_single_query_regression: f64,
}

impl Slot {
    pub fn load(dir: &Path) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let path = dir.join("slot.json");
        let text = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        let slot: Slot = serde_json::from_str(&text)
            .map_err(|e| format!("{}: {e}", path.display()))?;
        if slot.workloads.public.kind != "tpch" {
            return Err(format!(
                "public workload kind is {:?}; this harness only generates TPC-H",
                slot.workloads.public.kind
            ));
        }
        // The aggregate is not a knob the harness can quietly reinterpret. If a
        // slot asks for something else, refuse rather than report a median and
        // call it whatever the slot said.
        if slot.scoring.aggregate != "trimmed_median" {
            return Err(format!(
                "scoring aggregate is {:?}; only trimmed_median is implemented",
                slot.scoring.aggregate
            ));
        }
        Ok(slot)
    }
}
[package]
name = "slot-df-bridge"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "Apache-2.0"
description = "Conservative lowering between DataFusion LogicalPlan and the slot IR."

[dependencies]
slot-relalg = { path = "../relalg" }
datafusion = "50"
datafusion-common = "50"
datafusion-expr = "50"
//! Conservative lowering between a DataFusion `LogicalPlan` and the slot IR.
//!
//! # Why this file is the real trusted computing base
//!
//! Everything a miner proves is a statement about `Slot.Rel` under the bag
//! semantics in `lean/Slot/RelAlg.lean`. That proof transfers to DataFusion
//! only as far as this module's claim holds: that `lower` produces a `Rel`
//! meaning the same thing as the plan it came from, and `lift` produces a plan
//! meaning the same thing as the `Rel` it came from. No Lean theorem covers
//! that claim. It is defended three other ways:
//!
//! 1. **Conservatism.** `lower` returns `None` for anything the v1 fragment
//!    cannot express, and the caller then leaves that subtree exactly as it
//!    was. Being unable to express a node is never a licence to approximate
//!    it — most of the code below is refusals.
//! 2. **Scan identity.** `Rel::Scan { table }` is an index into a side table of
//!    the *original* `LogicalPlan` scan nodes. Lifting rebuilds from those
//!    nodes verbatim, so table sources, pushed-down filters and projections
//!    inside a scan are carried through untouched rather than re-derived.
//! 3. **Differential execution.** `crates/bench` runs every scored query with
//!    and without the rule and compares result sets. A bridge bug shows up as a
//!    wrong answer on a real workload, which is the only check that exercises
//!    the parts no proof reaches.
//!
//! Order-sensitivity is the trap to keep in mind while extending this file.
//! Bag equivalence is only a sound correctness notion for operators that do not
//! observe row order, so `Limit`, `Sort`, window functions and anything
//! downstream of them must stay unlowerable until the Lean semantics grows a
//! notion of order.

use std::sync::Arc;

use datafusion_common::arrow::datatypes::DataType;
use datafusion_common::{DFSchema, ExprSchema};
use datafusion_expr::ExprSchemable;
use datafusion_common::ScalarValue;
use datafusion_expr::{BinaryExpr, Expr, LogicalPlan, Operator};
use slot_relalg::{Rel, Scalar, Value};

/// The original scan nodes, indexed by the `table` field of `Rel::Scan`.
#[derive(Default, Clone)]
pub struct ScanTable {
    scans: Vec<Arc<LogicalPlan>>,
}

impl ScanTable {
    fn intern(&mut self, plan: &LogicalPlan) -> u32 {
        let index = self.scans.len() as u32;
        self.scans.push(Arc::new(plan.clone()));
        index
    }

    fn get(&self, index: u32) -> Option<&Arc<LogicalPlan>> {
        self.scans.get(index as usize)
    }

    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.scans.len()
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.scans.is_empty()
    }
}

/// Lower a plan into the v1 fragment, or decline.
///
/// The returned `ScanTable` must be paired with the returned `Rel`: indices are
/// only meaningful against the table they were interned into.
pub fn lower(plan: &LogicalPlan) -> Option<(Rel, ScanTable)> {
    let mut scans = ScanTable::default();
    let rel = lower_into(plan, &mut scans)?;
    Some((rel, scans))
}

fn lower_into(plan: &LogicalPlan, scans: &mut ScanTable) -> Option<Rel> {
    match plan {
        // A scan is opaque: whatever it already carries stays inside it.
        LogicalPlan::TableScan(_) => Some(Rel::Scan {
            width: plan.schema().fields().len() as u32,
            table: scans.intern(plan),
        }),

        LogicalPlan::Filter(filter) => {
            let input = lower_into(&filter.input, scans)?;
            let pred = lower_expr(&filter.predicate, &filter.input)?;
            Some(Rel::Filter { pred, input: Box::new(input) })
        }

        // v1 has no computed columns: a projection must be a pure permutation
        // or subset of its input's columns, otherwise the semantics in
        // `Slot.eval` (`cs.map (cellAt row)`) would not describe it.
        LogicalPlan::Projection(projection) => {
            let mut cols = Vec::with_capacity(projection.expr.len());
            for expr in &projection.expr {
                cols.push(column_index(expr, &projection.input)?);
            }
            let input = lower_into(&projection.input, scans)?;
            Some(Rel::Project { cols, input: Box::new(input) })
        }

        // Inner equijoins only, and only when the whole join condition can be
        // expressed as one predicate over the concatenated row. Outer joins
        // invent NULL rows, which `Slot.Rel.join` does not model.
        LogicalPlan::Join(join) => {
            if join.join_type != datafusion_expr::JoinType::Inner {
                return None;
            }
            let left_width = join.left.schema().fields().len() as u32;
            let left = lower_into(&join.left, scans)?;
            let right = lower_into(&join.right, scans)?;

            let mut conjuncts: Vec<Scalar> = Vec::new();
            for (l, r) in &join.on {
                let li = column_index(l, &join.left)?;
                let ri = column_index(r, &join.right)?;
                conjuncts.push(Scalar::Eq(
                    Box::new(Scalar::Col(li)),
                    Box::new(Scalar::Col(ri + left_width)),
                ));
            }
            if let Some(filter) = &join.filter {
                conjuncts.push(lower_expr_joined(filter, &join.left, &join.right, left_width)?);
            }
            let pred = conjuncts
                .into_iter()
                .reduce(|a, b| Scalar::And(Box::new(a), Box::new(b)))
                .unwrap_or(Scalar::Lit(Some(Value::Bool(true))));

            Some(Rel::Join { pred, left: Box::new(left), right: Box::new(right) })
        }

        // `UNION ALL` over exactly two inputs. DataFusion's `Union` is n-ary and
        // may be a distinct union; both are declined rather than folded, because
        // folding would have to assume associativity the IR has not proven.
        LogicalPlan::Union(union) if union.inputs.len() == 2 => {
            let left = lower_into(&union.inputs[0], scans)?;
            let right = lower_into(&union.inputs[1], scans)?;
            // `Option::==` would call two unrepresentable widths equal, so the
            // widths are required to exist before they are compared. Neither can
            // actually be unrepresentable here — both come from a DataFusion
            // schema — but a `lower` that depends on that is a `lower` that
            // breaks when someone widens the fragment.
            match (left.width(), right.width()) {
                (Some(l), Some(r)) if l == r => {}
                _ => return None,
            }
            Some(Rel::Union { left: Box::new(left), right: Box::new(right) })
        }

        // Everything else — aggregation, limit, sort, window, distinct, CTEs,
        // subquery aliases, DML — is out of the fragment.
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Positional index of a bare column reference within `input`'s schema.
fn column_index(expr: &Expr, input: &LogicalPlan) -> Option<u32> {
    let column = match expr {
        Expr::Column(c) => c,
        _ => return None,
    };
    input.schema().index_of_column(column).ok().map(|i| i as u32)
}

fn lower_expr(expr: &Expr, input: &LogicalPlan) -> Option<Scalar> {
    lower_expr_with(expr, &|c| {
        input.schema().index_of_column(c).ok().map(|i| i as u32)
    })
}

fn lower_expr_joined(
    expr: &Expr,
    left: &LogicalPlan,
    right: &LogicalPlan,
    left_width: u32,
) -> Option<Scalar> {
    lower_expr_with(expr, &|c| {
        if let Ok(i) = left.schema().index_of_column(c) {
            return Some(i as u32);
        }
        right.schema().index_of_column(c).ok().map(|i| i as u32 + left_width)
    })
}

fn lower_expr_with(
    expr: &Expr,
    resolve: &dyn Fn(&datafusion_common::Column) -> Option<u32>,
) -> Option<Scalar> {
    match expr {
        Expr::Column(c) => Some(Scalar::Col(resolve(c)?)),
        Expr::Literal(value, _) => Some(Scalar::Lit(lower_literal(value)?)),
        Expr::Not(inner) => Some(Scalar::Not(Box::new(lower_expr_with(inner, resolve)?))),
        Expr::IsNull(inner) => Some(Scalar::IsNull(Box::new(lower_expr_with(inner, resolve)?))),
        Expr::IsNotNull(inner) => Some(Scalar::Not(Box::new(Scalar::IsNull(Box::new(
            lower_expr_with(inner, resolve)?,
        ))))),
        Expr::BinaryExpr(BinaryExpr { left, op, right }) => {
            let l = Box::new(lower_expr_with(left, resolve)?);
            let r = Box::new(lower_expr_with(right, resolve)?);
            match op {
                Operator::Eq => Some(Scalar::Eq(l, r)),
                Operator::Lt => Some(Scalar::Lt(l, r)),
                // `a > b` is `b < a`; the slot IR has one ordering operator.
                Operator::Gt => Some(Scalar::Lt(r, l)),
                Operator::And => Some(Scalar::And(l, r)),
                Operator::Or => Some(Scalar::Or(l, r)),
                // `<=`, `>=`, `!=` are deliberately absent: expressing them as
                // `Not (Lt ..)` is wrong under three-valued logic, because
                // `NOT NULL` is `NULL` rather than `TRUE`.
                _ => None,
            }
        }
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn lower_literal(value: &ScalarValue) -> Option<Option<Value>> {
    match value {
        ScalarValue::Null => Some(None),
        ScalarValue::Boolean(b) => Some(b.map(Value::Bool)),
        ScalarValue::Int8(v) => Some(v.map(|n| Value::Int(n as i64))),
        ScalarValue::Int16(v) => Some(v.map(|n| Value::Int(n as i64))),
        ScalarValue::Int32(v) => Some(v.map(|n| Value::Int(n as i64))),
        ScalarValue::Int64(v) => Some(v.map(Value::Int)),
        // `Utf8View` is the same logical type as `Utf8` with a different
        // physical layout, and it is what DataFusion 50 gives string columns
        // read from Parquet. Omitting it made every string predicate in TPC-H
        // unlowerable, which is how M1 found it.
        ScalarValue::Utf8(s) | ScalarValue::LargeUtf8(s) | ScalarValue::Utf8View(s) => {
            Some(s.as_ref().map(|s| Value::Str(s.clone())))
        }
        // Dates are modelled as their epoch offset, which is not a widening.
        // `Date32` *is* a day count and `Date64` *is* a millisecond count, and
        // DataFusion compares both by comparing those integers, so `Slot.Value`
        // ordering on the offset agrees with date ordering exactly rather than
        // approximately. Type coercion guarantees both sides of a comparison
        // have the same date type before this sees them, so an offset in days
        // is never compared against one in milliseconds.
        //
        // Contrast the decimal case below: there the integer is a *scaled*
        // representation, so agreement would depend on both sides carrying the
        // same scale, which is a property of DataFusion's coercion rules rather
        // than of the values. That is an assumption the trusted computing base
        // should not be making, which is why it does not.
        ScalarValue::Date32(days) => Some(days.map(|d| Value::Int(d as i64))),
        ScalarValue::Date64(millis) => Some(millis.map(Value::Int)),
        // Decimals and floats are excluded until the Lean value domain models
        // their comparison semantics; silently widening them to `Int` would
        // make a proof about integers licence a rewrite over money columns.
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Rebuild a DataFusion plan from a rewritten `Rel`.
///
/// `lift` is only ever called on a `Rel` that `Slot.optimize_sound` guarantees
/// is bag-equivalent to the one `lower` produced, with the same width. It may
/// still fail — an out-of-range scan index, or a projection column that does
/// not exist — and failure means "keep the original plan", never "fail the
/// query".
pub fn lift(rel: &Rel, scans: &ScanTable) -> Option<LogicalPlan> {
    match rel {
        Rel::Scan { table, .. } => scans.get(*table).map(|plan| plan.as_ref().clone()),

        Rel::Filter { pred, input } => {
            let input = lift(input, scans)?;
            let predicate = lift_expr(pred, &input, None, 0)?;
            if !is_usable_predicate(&predicate, input.schema()) {
                return None;
            }
            datafusion_expr::LogicalPlanBuilder::from(input)
                .filter(predicate)
                .ok()?
                .build()
                .ok()
        }

        Rel::Project { cols, input } => {
            let input = lift(input, scans)?;
            let schema = input.schema();
            let mut exprs = Vec::with_capacity(cols.len());
            for index in cols {
                let field = schema.qualified_field(*index as usize);
                exprs.push(Expr::Column(datafusion_common::Column::from(field)));
            }
            datafusion_expr::LogicalPlanBuilder::from(input)
                .project(exprs)
                .ok()?
                .build()
                .ok()
        }

        Rel::Join { pred, left, right } => {
            let left = lift(left, scans)?;
            let right = lift(right, scans)?;
            let left_width = left.schema().fields().len() as u32;
            let condition = lift_expr(pred, &left, Some(&right), left_width)?;
            let joined = left.schema().join(right.schema()).ok()?;
            if !is_usable_predicate(&condition, &joined) {
                return None;
            }
            datafusion_expr::LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left)
                .join_on(right, datafusion_expr::JoinType::Inner, [condition])
                .ok()?
                .build()
                .ok()
        }

        Rel::Union { left, right } => {
            let left = lift(left, scans)?;
            let right = lift(right, scans)?;
            datafusion_expr::LogicalPlanBuilder::from(left).union(right).ok()?.build().ok()
        }
    }
}

fn lift_expr(
    scalar: &Scalar,
    left: &LogicalPlan,
    right: Option<&LogicalPlan>,
    left_width: u32,
) -> Option<Expr> {
    let column = |index: u32| -> Option<Expr> {
        if index < left_width || right.is_none() {
            let schema = left.schema();
            if index as usize >= schema.fields().len() {
                return None;
            }
            Some(Expr::Column(datafusion_common::Column::from(
                schema.qualified_field(index as usize),
            )))
        } else {
            let schema = right?.schema();
            let offset = (index - left_width) as usize;
            if offset >= schema.fields().len() {
                return None;
            }
            Some(Expr::Column(datafusion_common::Column::from(schema.qualified_field(offset))))
        }
    };
    let binary = |op: Operator, a: &Scalar, b: &Scalar| -> Option<Expr> {
        let mut lhs = lift_expr(a, left, right, left_width)?;
        let mut rhs = lift_expr(b, left, right, left_width)?;
        retype_against_sibling(&mut lhs, &rhs, left, right);
        retype_against_sibling(&mut rhs, &lhs, left, right);
        Some(Expr::BinaryExpr(BinaryExpr { left: Box::new(lhs), op, right: Box::new(rhs) }))
    };
    match scalar {
        Scalar::Col(i) => column(*i),
        Scalar::Lit(cell) => Some(Expr::Literal(lift_literal(cell), None)),
        Scalar::Eq(a, b) => binary(Operator::Eq, a, b),
        Scalar::Lt(a, b) => binary(Operator::Lt, a, b),
        Scalar::And(a, b) => binary(Operator::And, a, b),
        Scalar::Or(a, b) => binary(Operator::Or, a, b),
        Scalar::Not(a) => Some(Expr::Not(Box::new(lift_expr(a, left, right, left_width)?))),
        Scalar::IsNull(a) => Some(Expr::IsNull(Box::new(lift_expr(a, left, right, left_width)?))),
    }
}

/// Whether a lifted predicate is one DataFusion can actually evaluate.
///
/// This check cannot be delegated. `Filter::try_new` validates the predicate's
/// type only on a *best effort*: it calls `get_type` and, when that **errors**,
/// skips the check and builds the node anyway — for correlated subqueries, whose
/// types genuinely cannot be resolved at construction time. An untypeable
/// predicate produced by a bad lift takes the same path, so the malformed plan is
/// accepted here and fails much later, during physical planning, as a failed
/// query rather than a declined rewrite.
///
/// That would break the one property `crates/df-rule-host` promises: every
/// failure degrades to "keep the original plan". A bridge bug must cost a lost
/// optimisation, never a lost query. So the type is resolved here, and anything
/// that does not resolve to a boolean is refused.
///
/// `Null` is accepted alongside `Boolean` because DataFusion accepts it too, as
/// a missing boolean — a filter whose predicate is the literal `NULL` keeps no
/// rows, which is what `Slot.truthy` says about it as well.
fn is_usable_predicate(predicate: &Expr, schema: &DFSchema) -> bool {
    matches!(predicate.get_type(schema), Ok(DataType::Boolean) | Ok(DataType::Null))
        && operands_agree(predicate, schema)
}

/// Whether every comparison in the predicate has operands of the same type.
///
/// Typing to `Boolean` is not enough. DataFusion's comparison coercion happily
/// types `Int64 < Int32`, so a literal this module failed to narrow produces a
/// plan that passes every check here and then fails the *query* later, in the
/// range analysis, with "Only intervals with the same data type are comparable".
/// Stages downstream of the optimizer assume the coercion the analyzer would have
/// applied, and the analyzer has already run.
///
/// So the requirement is the stronger one: operands agree, or one of them is a
/// `NULL` literal, which every stage does handle. Anything else is refused, and a
/// refusal costs a rewrite rather than a query. If this starts declining rewrites
/// it should be fixed by teaching `retype_against_sibling` the type, never by
/// weakening the check.
fn operands_agree(expr: &Expr, schema: &DFSchema) -> bool {
    match expr {
        Expr::BinaryExpr(BinaryExpr { left, op, right }) => {
            let agree = match op {
                Operator::And | Operator::Or => true,
                _ => {
                    let (l, r) = (left.get_type(schema), right.get_type(schema));
                    match (l, r) {
                        (Ok(DataType::Null), Ok(_)) | (Ok(_), Ok(DataType::Null)) => true,
                        (Ok(l), Ok(r)) => l == r,
                        _ => false,
                    }
                }
            };
            agree && operands_agree(left, schema) && operands_agree(right, schema)
        }
        Expr::Not(inner) | Expr::IsNull(inner) => operands_agree(inner, schema),
        _ => true,
    }
}

/// Give a literal the type of the column it is compared against.
///
/// `Slot.Value` is narrower than `ScalarValue`, so lifting on its own cannot
/// recover what a literal was lowered from: a `Date32` became an `Int` and comes
/// back as an `Int64`. Nothing unsound follows — the day count is the same
/// number — but `TypeCoercion` is an *analyzer* rule and has already run, so
/// nothing downstream will repair `l_shipdate > Int64(9497)`. The rebuilt plan
/// fails to type, `lift` returns `None`, and the rewrite is dropped: safe, and
/// invisible except as an error counter. Exactly the predicates that dates made
/// lowerable would stop being rewritten.
///
/// So the type is restored here, from the sibling column, and only where the
/// restoration is exact:
///
/// * an `Int` against a date column is that column's epoch offset, because that
///   is the only thing `lower` could have produced there;
/// * a `Str` against a view or large string column is the same string.
///
/// Anything else is left alone on purpose. If DataFusion cannot type it,
/// `Filter::try_new` rejects the plan and the caller keeps the original, which
/// is the conservative outcome. Coercing a literal to a type this function
/// cannot reproduce exactly — a decimal above all — would be the bridge
/// inventing a value, and that is the one thing it must never do.
fn retype_against_sibling(
    literal: &mut Expr,
    sibling: &Expr,
    left: &LogicalPlan,
    right: Option<&LogicalPlan>,
) {
    let Expr::Literal(value, metadata) = literal else {
        return;
    };
    let Expr::Column(column) = sibling else {
        return;
    };
    let Some(target) = column_data_type(column, left, right) else {
        return;
    };
    let retyped = match (&value, &target) {
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::Date32) => match i32::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(days) => ScalarValue::Date32(Some(days)),
            // Out of range for a date. Left as an `Int64`, so the plan fails to
            // type and the rewrite is dropped — the right outcome for a
            // predicate no date could have satisfied.
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::Date64) => ScalarValue::Date64(Some(*n)),
        // Narrower integers. `Slot.Value` has one integer type, so a comparison
        // against an `Int32` column comes back as an `Int64` and has to be
        // narrowed. Exact or not at all: `try_from` fails rather than truncating.
        //
        // This is the same bug as the date one, in a type the reference rule never
        // reached. It was worse, too: `Int64` against `Int32` *does* type-check,
        // because DataFusion's comparison coercion widens to `Int64`, so the guard
        // below passed and the plan was accepted -- and then a later stage failed
        // the query with "Only intervals with the same data type are comparable".
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::Int32) => match i32::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::Int32(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::Int16) => match i16::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::Int16(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::Int8) => match i8::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::Int8(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::UInt64) => match u64::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::UInt64(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::UInt32) => match u32::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::UInt32(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::UInt16) => match u16::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::UInt16(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Int64(Some(n)), DataType::UInt8) => match u8::try_from(*n) {
            Ok(v) => ScalarValue::UInt8(Some(v)),
            Err(_) => return,
        },
        (ScalarValue::Utf8(Some(s)), DataType::Utf8View) => ScalarValue::Utf8View(Some(s.clone())),
        (ScalarValue::Utf8(Some(s)), DataType::LargeUtf8) => {
            ScalarValue::LargeUtf8(Some(s.clone()))
        }
        _ => return,
    };
    *literal = Expr::Literal(retyped, metadata.clone());
}

/// The declared type of a lifted column reference, on whichever side of a join
/// it came from.
fn column_data_type(
    column: &datafusion_common::Column,
    left: &LogicalPlan,
    right: Option<&LogicalPlan>,
) -> Option<DataType> {
    if let Ok(data_type) = left.schema().data_type(column) {
        return Some(data_type.clone());
    }
    right?.schema().data_type(column).ok().cloned()
}

fn lift_literal(cell: &Option<Value>) -> ScalarValue {
    match cell {
        None => ScalarValue::Null,
        Some(Value::Bool(b)) => ScalarValue::Boolean(Some(*b)),
        Some(Value::Int(n)) => ScalarValue::Int64(Some(*n)),
        Some(Value::Str(s)) => ScalarValue::Utf8(Some(s.clone())),
    }
}
[package]
name = "slot-df-rule-host"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
license = "Apache-2.0"
description = "DataFusion OptimizerRule backed by an out-of-process Lean rule."

[dependencies]
slot-relalg = { path = "../relalg" }
slot-df-bridge = { path = "../df-bridge" }
datafusion = "50"
datafusion-common = "50"
datafusion-expr = "50"
datafusion-optimizer = "50"
//! A DataFusion `OptimizerRule` backed by the miner's Lean rule.
//!
//! The Lean rule runs out of process, behind a pipe, under whatever sandbox the
//! caller started it in. That costs a round trip per plan node group — tens of
//! microseconds against seconds of query execution, which is the whole reason
//! this design works: **the proved artifact is the shipped artifact.** There is
//! no extraction step, no re-implementation in Rust, and therefore no gap
//! between what was proved and what runs.
//!
//! Every failure mode here degrades to "keep the original plan":
//!
//! | failure | response |
//! |---|---|
//! | plan outside the v1 fragment | subtree unchanged |
//! | host process died or timed out | rule disabled for the rest of the session |
//! | malformed or `err` response | plan unchanged |
//! | returned plan has a different width | plan unchanged, counted as a violation |
//! | `lift` cannot rebuild the plan | plan unchanged |
//!
//! A width mismatch is the interesting one. `Slot.Sound` proves it cannot
//! happen, so observing it means the executed binary is not the proved rule —
//! a build or packaging bug, or tampering. It is counted separately and the
//! benchmark run is failed rather than merely degraded.

use std::io::{BufRead, BufReader, Write};
use std::process::{Child, ChildStdin, ChildStdout, Command, Stdio};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

use datafusion_common::tree_node::Transformed;
use datafusion_common::Result;
use datafusion_expr::LogicalPlan;
use datafusion_optimizer::{ApplyOrder, OptimizerConfig, OptimizerRule};
use slot_relalg::wire::{rewrite_request, rewrite_response};
use slot_relalg::Rel;

#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct RuleStats {
    pub attempts: AtomicU64,
    pub rewrites: AtomicU64,
    /// The bridge could not lower the node: it is outside the v1 fragment.
    pub declined: AtomicU64,
    /// The bridge lowered the node and the miner's rule chose not to rewrite it.
    ///
    /// Separate from `declined` because the two say completely different things
    /// to whoever is reading the report. All `declined` means the fragment does
    /// not reach this workload and the bridge is what to work on; all
    /// `unchanged` means the fragment reaches it fine and the rule is what to
    /// work on. Collapsing them into one counter hides which.
    pub unchanged: AtomicU64,
    /// The host did not answer, or answered something that is not a plan. A
    /// protocol failure, and the host is disabled for the rest of the session.
    pub errors: AtomicU64,
    /// The rule returned a different plan and `lift` could not rebuild it, or
    /// the rebuilt plan's schema drifted. Separate from `errors` because it says
    /// the *bridge* is the limit, not the host: the rewrite was real and was
    /// dropped. `docs/STATUS.md` records a bug that lived exactly in this gap.
    pub lift_failures: AtomicU64,
    /// Non-zero means the running artifact contradicts `Slot.Sound`. Treat any
    /// benchmark run with a non-zero count as void, not merely slow.
    pub width_violations: AtomicU64,
    pub host_micros: AtomicU64,
}

struct HostProcess {
    child: Child,
    stdin: ChildStdin,
    stdout: BufReader<ChildStdout>,
}

/// Ask the host the most trivial question there is and wait for the answer.
///
/// The plan is a bare scan, which no rule can rewrite, so the expected reply is
/// the request echoed back. Only the *shape* of the reply is checked: a rule is
/// entitled to leave a scan alone, and this is a liveness check, not a
/// correctness one.
///
/// Not routed through `ask`, so the counters and `host_micros` describe scored
/// work only.
fn warm_up(host: &mut HostProcess) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use std::io::{Error, ErrorKind};

    let probe = Rel::Scan { table: 0, width: 0 };
    let request = rewrite_request(0, &probe);
    writeln!(host.stdin, "{request}")?;
    host.stdin.flush()?;

    // A blocking read with no deadline of its own: the caller's process-level
    // timeout is what bounds this, because a `read_line` cannot be interrupted
    // without another thread and the sandbox already imposes a wall clock.
    let started = Instant::now();
    let mut line = String::new();
    let read = host.stdout.read_line(&mut line)?;
    if read == 0 {
        return Err(Error::new(
            ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof,
            "the rule host exited without answering; check LEAN_PATH and that \
             SlotEntry.olean is the miner's rather than the baseline's",
        ));
    }
    if started.elapsed() > STARTUP_TIMEOUT {
        return Err(Error::new(
            ErrorKind::TimedOut,
            format!("the rule host took longer than {STARTUP_TIMEOUT:?} to answer once"),
        ));
    }
    if rewrite_response(line.trim()).is_err() {
        return Err(Error::new(
            ErrorKind::InvalidData,
            format!("the rule host's first answer is not a plan: {}", line.trim()),
        ));
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub struct LeanRule {
    name: String,
    fuel: u32,
    max_plan_nodes: usize,
    timeout: Duration,
    host: Mutex<Option<HostProcess>>,
    pub stats: Arc<RuleStats>,
}

/// How long the host may take to become able to answer at all.
///
/// Deliberately unrelated to `timeout`. `lean --run` elaborates the host module
/// from source before it reads anything, which is a second or so, and that cost
/// is paid once per process rather than once per plan. Charging it to the
/// per-request budget made the *first* rewrite of a run fail on a slow machine
/// and, because a timeout disables the host permanently, silently cost every
/// rewrite after it too. The symptom was a rule that looked like it declined
/// everything.
const STARTUP_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30);

impl std::fmt::Debug for LeanRule {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("LeanRule").field("name", &self.name).field("fuel", &self.fuel).finish()
    }
}

impl LeanRule {
    /// Spawn the rule host. `command` is the already-sandboxed invocation; this
    /// crate deliberately does not build the sandbox itself, so that the
    /// benchmark harness and the validator can impose different policies
    /// without this code having an opinion about either.
    pub fn spawn(name: impl Into<String>, mut command: Command, fuel: u32) -> std::io::Result<Self> {
        let mut child = command
            .stdin(Stdio::piped())
            .stdout(Stdio::piped())
            .stderr(Stdio::null())
            .spawn()?;
        let stdin = child.stdin.take().expect("piped stdin");
        let stdout = BufReader::new(child.stdout.take().expect("piped stdout"));
        let mut host = HostProcess { child, stdin, stdout };

        // Return a host that has already answered once, so `ask`'s budget is
        // purely the cost of a rewrite. This also turns "the host cannot run at
        // all" -- a bad LEAN_PATH, a missing olean, a sandbox that denies exec --
        // into an error here rather than into a rule that quietly declines
        // everything for the rest of the process.
        warm_up(&mut host)?;

        Ok(Self {
            name: name.into(),
            fuel,
            max_plan_nodes: 4096,
            timeout: Duration::from_millis(250),
            host: Mutex::new(Some(host)),
            stats: Arc::new(RuleStats::default()),
        })
    }

    pub fn with_timeout(mut self, timeout: Duration) -> Self {
        self.timeout = timeout;
        self
    }

    /// Kill the host and refuse further rewrites. Called on any protocol
    /// failure: a half-spoken pipe cannot be resynchronised, and continuing
    /// would risk pairing one plan's request with another's response.
    fn disable(&self) {
        if let Ok(mut guard) = self.host.lock() {
            if let Some(mut host) = guard.take() {
                let _ = host.child.kill();
                let _ = host.child.wait();
            }
        }
    }

    fn ask(&self, request: &str) -> Option<String> {
        let started = Instant::now();
        let mut guard = self.host.lock().ok()?;
        let host = guard.as_mut()?;
        if writeln!(host.stdin, "{request}").is_err() || host.stdin.flush().is_err() {
            drop(guard);
            self.disable();
            return None;
        }
        let mut line = String::new();
        let read = host.stdout.read_line(&mut line);
        let elapsed = started.elapsed();
        self.stats.host_micros.fetch_add(elapsed.as_micros() as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
        match read {
            Ok(0) | Err(_) => {
                drop(guard);
                self.disable();
                None
            }
            Ok(_) if elapsed > self.timeout => {
                // The response arrived, but too late to be worth trusting the
                // process's pacing for the rest of the run.
                drop(guard);
                self.disable();
                None
            }
            Ok(_) => Some(line),
        }
    }
}

impl OptimizerRule for LeanRule {
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        &self.name
    }

    /// DataFusion drives the recursion, and `rewrite` therefore sees every node
    /// rather than only the root.
    ///
    /// This is not a tuning choice. `rewrite` does not recurse, so returning
    /// `None` here -- the trait's default -- means the rule is offered the root
    /// plan and nothing else. Every real query has something out of the v1
    /// fragment at its root: an aggregate, a sort, a limit. `lower` declines,
    /// the rule never fires, and the failure is silent -- it reads as "the rule
    /// found no improvement" rather than as "the rule was never asked". M1
    /// found exactly this.
    ///
    /// Top-down rather than bottom-up because `lower` already walks the whole
    /// subtree beneath the node it is given: the first node that lowers is the
    /// largest one, so the miner's rule sees the most context. Bottom-up would
    /// hand it the leaves first and a `repeatN` fixpoint would have to rebuild
    /// the context the traversal just threw away.
    fn apply_order(&self) -> Option<ApplyOrder> {
        Some(ApplyOrder::TopDown)
    }

    fn rewrite(
        &self,
        plan: LogicalPlan,
        _config: &dyn OptimizerConfig,
    ) -> Result<Transformed<LogicalPlan>> {
        self.stats.attempts.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);

        let Some((rel, scans)) = slot_df_bridge::lower(&plan) else {
            self.stats.declined.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
        };
        if rel.size() > self.max_plan_nodes {
            self.stats.declined.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
        }

        let Some(line) = self.ask(&rewrite_request(self.fuel, &rel)) else {
            self.stats.errors.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
        };
        let rewritten = match rewrite_response(line.trim()) {
            Ok(rewritten) => rewritten,
            Err(_) => {
                self.stats.errors.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
            }
        };

        // A response whose arity is not representable counts as a violation
        // rather than as a decline. `Slot.Sound` proves the rewritten plan has
        // the same width as the submitted one, and the submitted one's width came
        // from a real schema, so it is representable; an unrepresentable one
        // cannot have come from the proved rule. See `Rel::width`, whose `Option`
        // exists for this and is why the comparison cannot be written with `!=`.
        match (rewritten.width(), rel.width()) {
            (Some(new_width), Some(old_width)) if new_width == old_width => {}
            _ => {
                self.stats.width_violations.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
            }
        }
        if rewritten == rel {
            self.stats.unchanged.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return Ok(Transformed::no(plan));
        }

        match slot_df_bridge::lift(&rewritten, &scans) {
            // A rebuilt plan whose schema drifted is not the plan we proved
            // anything about; the enclosing operators are still bound to the
            // original field qualifiers.
            Some(lifted) if lifted.schema().has_equivalent_names_and_types(plan.schema()).is_ok() => {
                self.stats.rewrites.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                Ok(Transformed::yes(lifted))
            }
            _ => {
                self.stats.lift_failures.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                Ok(Transformed::no(plan))
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Drop for LeanRule {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.disable();
    }
}
[package]
name = "slot-relalg"
version = "0.1.0"
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
description = "The v1 slot plan IR and its wire codec, mirrored from lean/Slot/RelAlg.lean."

[dependencies]
//! Emit the shared wire corpus as rewrite requests, one per line.
//!
//! `just wire-roundtrip` pipes this into the Lean host and checks that every
//! response decodes back to the plan that was sent. With the baseline rule
//! loaded the host is the identity, so any difference is a codec divergence
//! between `crates/relalg` and `lean/SlotHost/Wire.lean` — the one place where
//! a silent disagreement would invalidate every proof above it.

use slot_relalg::wire::{rel_to_sexp, rewrite_request};
use slot_relalg::{Rel, Scalar, Value};

fn corpus() -> Vec<Rel> {
    let scan = |t, w| Rel::Scan { table: t, width: w };
    vec![
        scan(0, 3),
        Rel::Filter {
            pred: Scalar::Lt(Box::new(Scalar::Col(0)), Box::new(Scalar::Lit(Some(Value::Int(-10))))),
            input: Box::new(scan(7, 8)),
        },
        Rel::Project { cols: vec![2, 0, 5], input: Box::new(scan(7, 8)) },
        Rel::Project { cols: vec![], input: Box::new(scan(7, 8)) },
        Rel::Join {
            pred: Scalar::Eq(Box::new(Scalar::Col(0)), Box::new(Scalar::Col(3))),
            left: Box::new(scan(0, 3)),
            right: Box::new(Rel::Union { left: Box::new(scan(1, 2)), right: Box::new(scan(2, 2)) }),
        },
        Rel::Filter {
            pred: Scalar::And(
                Box::new(Scalar::IsNull(Box::new(Scalar::Col(1)))),
                Box::new(Scalar::Not(Box::new(Scalar::Lit(Some(Value::Str(
                    "a b (c) \u{00e9} \u{4e2d}".into(),
                )))))),
            ),
            input: Box::new(scan(3, 4)),
        },
        Rel::Filter { pred: Scalar::Lit(None), input: Box::new(scan(3, 4)) },
        Rel::Filter { pred: Scalar::Lit(Some(Value::Bool(false))), input: Box::new(scan(3, 4)) },
    ]
}

fn main() {
    let mode = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "requests".into());
    for rel in corpus() {
        match mode.as_str() {
            "plans" => println!("{}", rel_to_sexp(&rel).render()),
            _ => println!("{}", rewrite_request(0, &rel)),
        }
    }
}
//! The v1 slot plan IR, mirrored from `lean/Slot/RelAlg.lean`.
//!
//! This crate is **trusted**. Nothing above it can be more correct than the
//! claim that a `Rel` here means the same thing as the `Slot.Rel` the Lean
//! proof is about. It therefore carries no dependencies, no inference, and no
//! cleverness: the enum mirrors the inductive type constructor for
//! constructor, and the codec mirrors `lean/SlotHost/Wire.lean` arm for arm.
//!
//! `just wire-roundtrip` runs a shared corpus through both implementations and
//! diffs the rendered output, which is the only thing that keeps the two
//! honest as the fragment grows.

pub mod sexpr;
pub mod wire;

pub use sexpr::Sexp;

/// A non-null scalar. Mirrors `Slot.Value`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Value {
    Int(i64),
    Str(String),
    Bool(bool),
}

/// A column value; `None` is SQL `NULL`. Mirrors `Slot.Cell`.
pub type Cell = Option<Value>;

/// Scalar expressions over a positional row. Mirrors `Slot.Scalar`.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Scalar {
    Col(u32),
    Lit(Cell),
    Eq(Box<Scalar>, Box<Scalar>),
    Lt(Box<Scalar>, Box<Scalar>),
    And(Box<Scalar>, Box<Scalar>),
    Or(Box<Scalar>, Box<Scalar>),
    Not(Box<Scalar>),
    IsNull(Box<Scalar>),
}

/// The v1 plan fragment. Mirrors `Slot.Rel`.
///
/// Anything absent here — `LIMIT`, `ORDER BY`, aggregation, outer joins, window
/// functions — is absent on purpose. The bridge refuses to lower those nodes
/// rather than approximating them, because bag equivalence is not a sound
/// notion of correctness for order-sensitive operators.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Rel {
    Scan { table: u32, width: u32 },
    Filter { pred: Scalar, input: Box<Rel> },
    Project { cols: Vec<u32>, input: Box<Rel> },
    Join { pred: Scalar, left: Box<Rel>, right: Box<Rel> },
    Union { left: Box<Rel>, right: Box<Rel> },
}

impl Rel {
    /// Output arity, or `None` when the true arity does not fit in a `u32`.
    ///
    /// Mirrors `Slot.Rel.width`, and must agree with it: the host checks the
    /// returned plan's width against the submitted plan's, which is the same
    /// property `Slot.Sound` proves. That makes this the one function in the
    /// crate where a disagreement with the Lean definition is a soundness bug
    /// rather than a wrong answer, and `verify/Verify/RelAlg.lean` proves there
    /// is none: `width r = some w ↔ w = Slot.Rel.width r`.
    ///
    /// **`Option` is why that biconditional holds.** `Slot.Rel.width` is over
    /// `Nat` and cannot overflow; a `u32` sum can. This used to return `u32` and
    /// add with a bare `+`, and the widths reaching it are not bounded — a
    /// rewrite response is parsed by `rel_of_sexp`, which accepts any `u32` for
    /// a scan's width. `Join(Scan{w = u32::MAX}, Scan{w = 9})` therefore had a
    /// true width of 2^32 + 8 and computed one of 8, which is what the host
    /// compares. The plan is a different plan and the check said it was the same
    /// one. In a build with overflow checks the same expression panics inside
    /// `OptimizerRule::rewrite`, which fails the query rather than declining the
    /// rewrite.
    ///
    /// So `None` means "this plan has no representable arity", and every caller
    /// must treat it as a width violation: `Slot.Sound` says a rewritten plan
    /// has the same width as the plan it came from, and that width came from a
    /// real schema, so it is representable. `None` is therefore only reachable
    /// from a response that did not come from the proved rule — which is exactly
    /// what the width check exists to catch.
    pub fn width(&self) -> Option<u32> {
        match self {
            Rel::Scan { width, .. } => Some(*width),
            Rel::Filter { input, .. } => input.width(),
            Rel::Project { cols, .. } => u32::try_from(cols.len()).ok(),
            Rel::Join { left, right, .. } => left.width()?.checked_add(right.width()?),
            Rel::Union { left, .. } => left.width(),
        }
    }

    /// Node count, used to bound wire size and to reject absurd plans before
    /// they reach the rule host.
    pub fn size(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Rel::Scan { .. } => 1,
            Rel::Filter { input, .. } => 1 + input.size(),
            Rel::Project { input, .. } => 1 + input.size(),
            Rel::Join { left, right, .. } => 1 + left.size() + right.size(),
            Rel::Union { left, right } => 1 + left.size() + right.size(),
        }
    }
}
//! S-expression syntax, mirroring `lean/SlotHost/Sexp.lean`.
//!
//! Every atom this codec emits is drawn from `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`: keywords, decimal
//! numbers, and hex-encoded strings. There is nothing to escape, which is the
//! only reason a parser this short is safe.

#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Sexp {
    Atom(String),
    List(Vec<Sexp>),
}

impl Sexp {
    pub fn atom(s: impl Into<String>) -> Sexp {
        Sexp::Atom(s.into())
    }

    pub fn render(&self) -> String {
        let mut out = String::new();
        self.render_into(&mut out);
        out
    }

    fn render_into(&self, out: &mut String) {
        match self {
            Sexp::Atom(s) => out.push_str(s),
            Sexp::List(xs) => {
                out.push('(');
                for (i, x) in xs.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i > 0 {
                        out.push(' ');
                    }
                    x.render_into(out);
                }
                out.push(')');
            }
        }
    }

    /// Parse exactly one s-expression. Trailing content is an error: a
    /// truncated or doubled frame must never decode to something plausible.
    pub fn parse(input: &str) -> Result<Sexp, String> {
        let tokens = tokenize(input);
        let mut pos = 0usize;
        let value = parse_one(&tokens, &mut pos)?;
        if pos != tokens.len() {
            return Err("trailing tokens".into());
        }
        Ok(value)
    }
}

fn tokenize(input: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut tokens = Vec::new();
    let mut current = String::new();
    for c in input.chars() {
        match c {
            '(' | ')' => {
                if !current.is_empty() {
                    tokens.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
                }
                tokens.push(c.to_string());
            }
            c if c.is_whitespace() => {
                if !current.is_empty() {
                    tokens.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
                }
            }
            c => current.push(c),
        }
    }
    if !current.is_empty() {
        tokens.push(current);
    }
    tokens
}

/// Recursion here is bounded by the plan-size check the host applies before
/// decoding, and by `MAX_DEPTH` for anything that slips past it.
const MAX_DEPTH: usize = 512;

fn parse_one(tokens: &[String], pos: &mut usize) -> Result<Sexp, String> {
    parse_at(tokens, pos, 0)
}

fn parse_at(tokens: &[String], pos: &mut usize, depth: usize) -> Result<Sexp, String> {
    if depth > MAX_DEPTH {
        return Err("nesting too deep".into());
    }
    let token = tokens.get(*pos).ok_or("unexpected end of input")?;
    if token == ")" {
        return Err("unexpected )".into());
    }
    if token != "(" {
        *pos += 1;
        return Ok(Sexp::Atom(token.clone()));
    }
    *pos += 1;
    let mut items = Vec::new();
    loop {
        let next = tokens.get(*pos).ok_or("unterminated list")?;
        if next == ")" {
            *pos += 1;
            return Ok(Sexp::List(items));
        }
        items.push(parse_at(tokens, pos, depth + 1)?);
    }
}
//! `Rel` ⟷ s-expression, mirroring `lean/SlotHost/Wire.lean` arm for arm.
//!
//! Strings are hex-encoded UTF-8 so that no atom can contain a delimiter.

use crate::{Cell, Rel, Scalar, Sexp, Value};

pub fn encode_hex(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len() * 2);
    for byte in s.as_bytes() {
        out.push(char::from_digit((byte >> 4) as u32, 16).unwrap());
        out.push(char::from_digit((byte & 0xf) as u32, 16).unwrap());
    }
    out
}

pub fn decode_hex(s: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
    if s.len() % 2 != 0 {
        return Err("odd-length hex string".into());
    }
    let bytes: Result<Vec<u8>, String> = s
        .as_bytes()
        .chunks(2)
        .map(|pair| {
            let hi = (pair[0] as char).to_digit(16).ok_or("bad hex digit")?;
            let lo = (pair[1] as char).to_digit(16).ok_or("bad hex digit")?;
            Ok((hi * 16 + lo) as u8)
        })
        .collect();
    String::from_utf8(bytes?).map_err(|_| "hex string is not valid UTF-8".into())
}

fn cell_to_sexp(c: &Cell) -> Sexp {
    match c {
        None => Sexp::atom("null"),
        Some(Value::Int(n)) => Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("int"), Sexp::atom(n.to_string())]),
        // An empty string hex-encodes to an empty atom, and an empty atom does
        // not survive `render` -> `tokenize`: the tokenizer emits nothing for it,
        // so `(str )` comes back as `(str)` and fails to decode. Both codecs did
        // that identically, so it cost a rewrite rather than an answer -- but a
        // representable value that cannot cross the wire is still a defect. A
        // one-element `(str)` is the empty string, and no empty atom is ever
        // emitted. `lean/SlotHost/Wire.lean` mirrors this.
        Some(Value::Str(s)) => {
            let hex = encode_hex(s);
            if hex.is_empty() {
                Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("str")])
            } else {
                Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("str"), Sexp::atom(hex)])
            }
        }
        Some(Value::Bool(b)) => {
            Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("bool"), Sexp::atom(if *b { "1" } else { "0" })])
        }
    }
}

fn scalar_to_sexp(s: &Scalar) -> Sexp {
    let binary = |tag: &str, a: &Scalar, b: &Scalar| {
        Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom(tag), scalar_to_sexp(a), scalar_to_sexp(b)])
    };
    match s {
        Scalar::Col(i) => Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("col"), Sexp::atom(i.to_string())]),
        Scalar::Lit(c) => Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("lit"), cell_to_sexp(c)]),
        Scalar::Eq(a, b) => binary("eq", a, b),
        Scalar::Lt(a, b) => binary("lt", a, b),
        Scalar::And(a, b) => binary("and", a, b),
        Scalar::Or(a, b) => binary("or", a, b),
        Scalar::Not(a) => Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("not"), scalar_to_sexp(a)]),
        Scalar::IsNull(a) => Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("isnull"), scalar_to_sexp(a)]),
    }
}

pub fn rel_to_sexp(r: &Rel) -> Sexp {
    match r {
        Rel::Scan { table, width } => Sexp::List(vec![
            Sexp::atom("scan"),
            Sexp::atom(table.to_string()),
            Sexp::atom(width.to_string()),
        ]),
        Rel::Filter { pred, input } => Sexp::List(vec![
            Sexp::atom("filter"),
            scalar_to_sexp(pred),
            rel_to_sexp(input),
        ]),
        Rel::Project { cols, input } => Sexp::List(vec![
            Sexp::atom("project"),
            Sexp::List(cols.iter().map(|c| Sexp::atom(c.to_string())).collect()),
            rel_to_sexp(input),
        ]),
        Rel::Join { pred, left, right } => Sexp::List(vec![
            Sexp::atom("join"),
            scalar_to_sexp(pred),
            rel_to_sexp(left),
            rel_to_sexp(right),
        ]),
        Rel::Union { left, right } => {
            Sexp::List(vec![Sexp::atom("union"), rel_to_sexp(left), rel_to_sexp(right)])
        }
    }
}

fn atom<'a>(s: &'a Sexp) -> Result<&'a str, String> {
    match s {
        Sexp::Atom(a) => Ok(a),
        Sexp::List(_) => Err("expected an atom, found a list".into()),
    }
}

fn nat(s: &Sexp) -> Result<u32, String> {
    atom(s)?.parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| format!("not a natural number: {}", s.render()))
}

fn cell_of_sexp(s: &Sexp) -> Result<Cell, String> {
    match s {
        Sexp::Atom(a) if a == "null" => Ok(None),
        Sexp::List(xs) => match xs.as_slice() {
            [Sexp::Atom(tag), v] if tag == "int" => Ok(Some(Value::Int(
                atom(v)?.parse::<i64>().map_err(|_| "not an integer".to_string())?,
            ))),
            [Sexp::Atom(tag)] if tag == "str" => Ok(Some(Value::Str(String::new()))),
            [Sexp::Atom(tag), Sexp::Atom(h)] if tag == "str" => {
                Ok(Some(Value::Str(decode_hex(h)?)))
            }
            [Sexp::Atom(tag), Sexp::Atom(b)] if tag == "bool" && (b == "0" || b == "1") => {
                Ok(Some(Value::Bool(b == "1")))
            }
            _ => Err(format!("not a cell: {}", s.render())),
        },
        _ => Err(format!("not a cell: {}", s.render())),
    }
}

pub fn scalar_of_sexp(s: &Sexp) -> Result<Scalar, String> {
    let items = match s {
        Sexp::List(xs) => xs,
        Sexp::Atom(_) => return Err(format!("not a scalar: {}", s.render())),
    };
    match items.as_slice() {
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), v] if tag == "col" => Ok(Scalar::Col(nat(v)?)),
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), c] if tag == "lit" => Ok(Scalar::Lit(cell_of_sexp(c)?)),
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a, b] if tag == "eq" => {
            Ok(Scalar::Eq(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?), Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(b)?)))
        }
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a, b] if tag == "lt" => {
            Ok(Scalar::Lt(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?), Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(b)?)))
        }
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a, b] if tag == "and" => {
            Ok(Scalar::And(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?), Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(b)?)))
        }
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a, b] if tag == "or" => {
            Ok(Scalar::Or(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?), Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(b)?)))
        }
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a] if tag == "not" => Ok(Scalar::Not(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?))),
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), a] if tag == "isnull" => {
            Ok(Scalar::IsNull(Box::new(scalar_of_sexp(a)?)))
        }
        _ => Err(format!("not a scalar: {}", s.render())),
    }
}

pub fn rel_of_sexp(s: &Sexp) -> Result<Rel, String> {
    let items = match s {
        Sexp::List(xs) => xs,
        Sexp::Atom(_) => return Err(format!("not a plan: {}", s.render())),
    };
    match items.as_slice() {
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), t, w] if tag == "scan" => {
            Ok(Rel::Scan { table: nat(t)?, width: nat(w)? })
        }
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), p, r] if tag == "filter" => Ok(Rel::Filter {
            pred: scalar_of_sexp(p)?,
            input: Box::new(rel_of_sexp(r)?),
        }),
        [Sexp::Atom(tag), Sexp::List(cs), r] if tag == "project" => Ok(Rel::Project {
